why_wrong.C: Money duration is in currency; key-rate durations are still percentage-style curve sensitivities, and they are not “identical to money duration.”

FI-139.zh: 關鍵利率duration 是只動一個天期的即期、其他不動，用來抓非平行風險。每個 即期都同樣移動時，加總等於有效存續期間。它不是MacDur/2，也不是貨幣duration。
FI-139.core_idea: Key-rate duration is the response to one maturity’s spot, others fixed; the sum equals effective duration when every spot shifts equally
FI-139.study_section: Modified, effective, and money duration ｜修正、有效與貨幣存續期間
FI-139.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。
FI-139.subtopic: 7.4 Modified, effective, and money duration ｜修正、有效與貨幣存續期間

FI-140.reasoning: Reasoning: Analytical duration comes from the formula and treats yield and spread as independent; empirical duration is measured from observed price–yield history.

why_wrong.A: The definitions are reversed in that choice, and analytical is not “always key-rate.”
why_wrong.C: PVBP is a 1 bp money change, not the analytical/empirical split.

FI-140.zh: 分析型duration 來自公式，把殖利率與利差當成獨立。實證duration 來自實際價 格－殖利率歷史。不是PVBP 的兩個別名。
FI-140.core_idea: Analytical duration treats yield and spread as independent; empirical duration is from price–yield history
FI-140.study_section: Modified, effective, and money duration ｜修正、有效與貨幣存續期間
FI-140.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。
FI-140.subtopic: 7.4 Modified, effective, and money duration ｜修正、有效與貨幣存續期間

FI-141.reasoning: Reasoning: Embedded options make expected cash flows interest-rate dependent. Effective duration is used. When the option is economically relevant, effective duration can differ materially and is often reduced. Analyze by type and by region — not one slogan for every embedded option.

why_wrong.A: Options do not “always” lengthen duration; a callable at low yields can flatten upside.
why_wrong.C: The chapter explicitly rejects an unconditional callable-and-putable shortening rule.

FI-141.zh: 選擇權變得划算時，有效duration 常常變短，但要看是call 還是put、當時利率 在哪。不要背「有嵌入選擇權＝duration 一定比較短」。
FI-141.core_idea: Do not collapse callable and putable into one “embedded options shorten duration” rule
FI-141.study_section: Modified, effective, and money duration ｜修正、有效與貨幣存續期間
FI-141.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。
FI-141.subtopic: 7.4 Modified, effective, and money duration ｜修正、有效與貨幣存續期間

FI-142.reasoning: Reasoning: ApproxConv = (101.80 + 96.40 - 2×99.00) / (0.0052 × 99) = (198.20 - 198.00) / 0.002475 = 0.20 / 0.002475 = 80.8. Annual convexity is a whole number in that units convention, not a percentage. Option-free convexity is positive. Given: PV0=99; PV-=101.80; PV+=96.40; ∆y=50 bp. Asked: Approximate convexity. Formula: (101.80 + 96.40 −198)/(0.0052 × 99) Variables: Use decimal ∆y. Why this formula: Second-order curvature from two equal bumps. Large positive curvature: the up-move (101.80) exceeds the down-move (96.40) in distance from 99. Reasonableness check: Negative would be the callable-at-low-yield shape, not this pair of prices. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。

why_wrong.A: Puts a minus on option-free convexity.
why_wrong.B: Drops a factor of 10 in the (∆y)2 scaling.

FI-142.zh: 近似凸性＝(降息價+ 升息價-2× 原價)/((∆y)2× 原價) ＝0.20/0.002475 ＝80.8。 option-free 為正。不要當百分比，也不要加負號。
FI-142.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。

FI-143.reasoning: Reasoning: %∆P = -4.00×0.01 + ½×22×(0.01)2 = -4.00% + 0.11% = -3.89%. Convexity always adds a positive adjustment for an option-free bond, which is why the duration-only estimate overstates the loss when yields rise. Given: ModDur=4.00; Conv=22; ∆y=+0.01; option-free. Asked: % price change with convexity. Formula: −4.00 × 0.01 + 1 2 × 22 × 0.0001 Variables: Decimal yields; convexity is a whole number in this convention. Why this formula: Slope plus curvature. The (∆y)2 term is positive for option-free convexity. Duration-only -4.00% overstates the loss; convexity gives 11 bp back. Reasonableness check: -4.00% dropped convexity. -4.11% signed convexity wrong. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。

why_wrong.B: Duration only: -4.00 × 0.01 = -4.00%, dropping convexity on a large move.
why_wrong.C: Subtracts the convexity term: -4.00% - 0.11% = -4.11%.

FI-143.zh: -4% 是只有duration 的切線。加上½×22×0.0001 ＝+0.11%，估計跌幅收斂到 3.89%。option-free 的凸性項永遠是正的，升息時duration-only 會高估損失。
FI-143.core_idea: %∆P = -ModDur×∆y + ½ Conv (∆y)2; convexity always adds a positive adjustment for optionfree
FI-143.exam_trap: Signing convexity, or dropping it on a large yield move
FI-143.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。

FI-144.reasoning: Reasoning: %∆P = -3.20×(-0.008) + ½×14.5×(0.008)2 = +2.56% + 7.25×0.000064 = +2.56% + 0.046% = +2.61%. Duration-only understates the gain when yields fall. Use decimal yields. Given: ModDur=3.20; Conv=14.5; ∆y=-0.008. Asked: % price change. Formula: −3.20 × (−0.008) + 1 2 × 14.5 × 0.0082 Variables: ∆y negative when yields fall. Why this formula: The convexity term uses (∆y)2 so it stays positive and adds to the duration gain. The extra 5 bp versus +2.56% is the curvature the tangent misses. Reasonableness check: +2.56% is duration-only. -2.56% flipped the yield-fall sign. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。

why_wrong.B: Duration only: -3.20 × (-0.008) = +2.56%, dropping convexity so the gain is understated.
why_wrong.C: Keeps a minus on the whole result as if yields rose.

FI-144.zh: 降息80 bp：duration 貢獻+2.56%，凸性再加約+0.05%，合計+2.61%。只乘 duration 會低估漲幅。不要整題留負號。
FI-144.core_idea: When yields fall, duration-only understates the gain; convexity adds more upside
FI-144.exam_trap: Signing convexity, or dropping it on a large yield move
FI-144.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。

FI-145.reasoning: Reasoning: Positive convexity means the percentage price increase from a yield drop exceeds the percentage price decrease from an equal yield rise. Reversing that inequality is the option-free trap.

why_wrong.B: Equal percentage changes is the duration tangent, which is why the convexity adjustment exists.
why_wrong.C: Smaller increase than decrease is the negative-convexity (callable, low-yield) shape.

FI-145.zh: Option-free 正凸性：同樣60 bp，跌息漲得比較多。漲得比較少是callable 在低殖 利率的負凸性。兩邊一樣是duration 切線。
FI-145.core_idea: Option-free: the % price increase from a yield drop exceeds the % decrease from an equal yield rise
FI-145.exam_trap: Signing convexity, or dropping it on a large yield move
FI-145.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。

FI-146.reasoning: Reasoning: Option-free bonds have positive convexity. Callable bonds at low yields, when the call is likely, can show negative convexity because price upside is capped. Putable bonds should not be memorized as negative convexity. Analyze by option type and rate region.

why_wrong.A: Option-free bonds have positive convexity.
why_wrong.C: The chapter rejects “embedded option = negative convexity” as a false rule, especially for putables.

FI-146.zh: Callable 在低殖利率、很可能被贖回時，上漲被call price 卡住，凸性可以變負。 Putable 不要直接背成負凸性。Option-free 是正凸性。
FI-146.core_idea: A callable at low yields can show negative convexity; do not extend that to every embedded option
FI-146.exam_trap: Signing convexity, or dropping it on a large yield move
FI-146.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。

FI-147.reasoning: Reasoning: Bondholders prefer more convexity, other things equal — more gain when yields fall, less loss when yields rise. For option-free bonds, higher YTM, lower duration.

why_wrong.A: The chapter’s preference is more convexity, other things equal — not less.
why_wrong.B: Duration is the tangent; it is not exact for a large ∆y, which is why convexity exists.

FI-147.zh: 其他條件相同，持有人喜歡更大的正凸性：跌息多賺、升息少賠。Duration 只是 切線，大∆y 並不精確。
FI-147.core_idea: Bondholders prefer more convexity, other things equal
FI-147.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。

FI-148.reasoning: Reasoning: Duration-only %∆P is a tangent. For a large ∆y the missing ½ Conv (∆y)2 term is the gap between the line and the curve. For option-free positive convexity, the tangent overstates the loss when yields rise and understates the gain when yields fall.

why_wrong.A: Convexity reduces the loss versus the tangent; it does not enlarge it for optionfree bonds.
why_wrong.C: Duration is first-order (the tangent), not second-order accurate.

FI-148.zh: 升息時，duration 切線會高估跌幅；少掉的凸性項是正的，實際跌得比較少。不 是凸性讓虧損變大。
FI-148.core_idea: Duration-only overstates the loss when yields rise on an option-free bond
FI-148.exam_trap: Signing convexity, or dropping it on a large yield move
FI-148.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。

FI-149.reasoning: Reasoning: Use decimal yields. Annual convexity is a whole number in that units convention (about 9.89 for the 3-year 6% par bond with 50 bp shocks), not a percentage. For a 100 bp increase: duration -2.67% plus ½×9.89×(0.01)2 = +0.05% gives -2.62%.

why_wrong.A: Money duration is AnnModDur × PV, not convexity.
why_wrong.B: Using 100 instead of 0.01 in (∆y)2 explodes the term. Convexity is not itself a percent.

FI-149.zh: 凸性約9.89 不是百分比；∆y 要用小數0.01。½×9.89×0.0001 ＝0.05%。若把∆y 打成100，數字會爆掉。
FI-149.core_idea: Use decimal yields in the convexity formula; convexity is a whole number in that convention
FI-149.exam_trap: Signing convexity, or dropping it on a large yield move
FI-149.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。

FI-150.reasoning: Reasoning: For a option-free bond: higher YTM, lower duration. Positive convexity remains: the percentage increase from a yield drop still exceeds the percentage decrease from an equal rise.

why_wrong.A: Higher YTM lowers duration for option-free bonds; it does not raise it.
why_wrong.B: Negative convexity is the callable-at-low-yield story, not the definition of a higher yield on an option-free bond.

FI-150.zh: Option-free：殖利率愈高，duration 愈低（曲線變平），但凸性仍讓漲跌不對稱。 負凸性不是「殖利率變高」的定義。
FI-150.core_idea: For option-free bonds, higher YTM, lower duration — the curve flattens as yield rises
FI-150.exam_trap: Reversing the coupon, yield, or maturity effect on duration
FI-150.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。

FI-151.reasoning: Reasoning: Do not memorize putable as negative convexity. A put can support price when yields rise (holder-friendly). Analyze by type and region. Negative convexity is the callable-at-low-yield case.

why_wrong.A: A put is not a call cap, and “every embedded option is negative convexity” is the false rule.
why_wrong.B: Puts do not cancel convexity to zero by definition.

FI-151.zh: Putable 不要自動當成負凸性。高殖利率、put 不值钱時，行為可以很接近optionfree。負凸性那條是低殖利率的callable。
FI-151.core_idea: A putable’s convexity is not automatically negative
FI-151.exam_trap: Signing convexity, or dropping it on a large yield move
FI-151.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。

FI-152.reasoning: Reasoning: Expected-loss rate = PD × LGD rate = 0.03 × 0.45 = 0.0135 = 1.35% = 135 bp. LGD rate = 1 - recovery. Do not write LGD sometimes as 45% and sometimes as a dollar amount without saying which one. Given: PD=3%; LGD rate=45%. Asked: Expected-loss rate. Formula: 0.03 × 0.45 Variables: LGD rate is a percentage (1 - RR), not a money amount. Why this formula: EL rate is the probability-weighted loss fraction. 135 bp of expected loss per unit of exposure, before any risk premium. Reasonableness check: 45% is LGD, not EL. 3% is PD, which would be EL only if LGD = 100%. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。

why_wrong.B: Reports LGD as if it were already EL.
why_wrong.C: Reports PD as if recovery were zero and EL = PD.

FI-152.zh: 預期損失率＝PD×LGD rate ＝3%×45% ＝1.35%。45% 是違約後還損失的比 例，不是EL。3% 是違約機率，回收不是零。
FI-152.core_idea: EL rate = PD × LGD rate; keep the percentage distinct from the money amount
FI-152.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。

FI-153.reasoning: Reasoning: LGD rate = 1 - 0.55 = 45%. LGD amount = EE × 0.45 = 90. EL amount = PD × EE × LGD rate = 0.03 × 200 × 0.45 = 2.70. EL rate = 0.03 × 0.45 = 1.35%. Distinguish rate versus amount. Given: EE=200; PD=3%; RR=55%. Asked: Expected-loss amount. Formula: 0.03 × 200 × 0.45 Variables: LGD rate = 1-RR; LGD amount = EE×LGD rate; EL amount also multiplies by PD. Why this formula: EL is the probability-weighted money loss, not the loss-if-default alone. On average you lose 2.70; if default occurs you lose 90. Reasonableness check: 90 skipped PD. 6 skipped LGD (assumed zero recovery). 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。
FI-153.steps: ①LGD rate = 45%. ②LGD amount = 90 (if default occurs). ③EL amount = 0.03 × 90 = 2.70.

why_wrong.B: Drops PD: LGD amount = 200 × (1 - 0.55) = 90, reported as EL.
why_wrong.C: Uses PD × EE and skips LGD: 0.03 × 200 = 6.

FI-153.zh: 回收55%，LGD rate ＝45%。EL 金額＝3%×200×45% ＝2.70。90 是一旦違約 的損失金額（還沒乘PD）。6 是假設全損。
FI-153.core_idea: LGD amount = EE × loss severity; EL amount = PD × EE × loss severity
FI-153.exam_trap: Confusing PD, LGD, EL rate, and EL amount
FI-153.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。

FI-154.reasoning: Reasoning: Loss severity / LGD rate = 1 - RR. Recovery 60% ⇒LGD rate 40%. Keep the percentage (rate) distinct from the money amount. Given: RR=60%. Asked: LGD rate. Formula: 1 −0.60 = 0.40 Variables: RR is the fraction recovered if default occurs. Why this formula: LGD is the complementary fraction lost. Forty cents of each exposure dollar is lost in default, given this recovery. Reasonableness check: 60% is recovery. EL still needs PD. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。

why_wrong.B: EL rate = PD × LGD rate = PD × 40%, not 60% × PD unless LGD was misread as recovery.
why_wrong.C: 60% is the recovery rate, not LGD.

FI-154.zh: 回收60%，違約損失率就是40%。不要把回收率貼上LGD 的標籤。EL rate 還要 再乘PD。
FI-154.core_idea: LGD rate = 1 - recovery; do not relabel recovery as LGD
FI-154.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。

FI-155.reasoning: Reasoning: EL rate = 0.015 × 0.60 = 0.90% = 90 bp. Spread 70 < 90, so not fairly compensated on that simplified test. An observed spread can also embed a credit-risk premium, liquidity, uncertainty, and technicals; that does not change a stem that says to use expected loss as the required compensation. Given: PD=1.50%; LGD rate=60%; spread=70 bp; use EL as required compensation. Asked: Fairly compensated on that test? Formula: 0.015 × 0.60 = 0.0090 Variables: Compare spread with EL rate, not with PD. Why this formula: The stem explicitly uses expected loss as the required compensation. The simplified test fails; a real spread can still contain extra premia, but the stem forbids using that as a rescue. Reasonableness check: 70>1.50 compared the wrong pair. Recovery is already in LGD. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。
FI-155.steps: ①EL rate = 90 bp. ②70 < 90 ⇒not fairly compensated on that test.
FI-155.final_answer: Not fairly compensated (90 bp EL vs 70 bp spread)

why_wrong.A: Compares the spread with PD instead of with PD × LGD.
why_wrong.C: Positive recovery is already inside the 60% LGD; it does not by itself make 70 bp enough.

FI-155.zh: EL rate ＝1.5%×60% ＝90 bp > 70 bp，用題幹指定的簡化測試是補償不足。選 70>1.5 是拿利差去跟PD 比。回收為正已經寫在60% LGD 裡。
FI-155.core_idea: If the question says to use EL as required compensation, compare the spread with the EL rate
FI-155.exam_trap: Comparing the credit spread with PD instead of EL rate
FI-155.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。

FI-156.reasoning: Reasoning: When a question explicitly says to use expected loss as the required compensation, compare the spread with the expected-loss rate. Otherwise remember the spread can contain more than EL.

why_wrong.B: The chapter calls it a simplified exercise, not an identity.
why_wrong.C: LGD is central to EL; it is not unused.

FI-156.zh: 利差＝PD×LGD 只是簡化練習。真實利差還可能含風險溢酬、流動性、不確定 性與技術因素。題目若明寫用EL 當補償，才這樣比。
FI-156.core_idea: The observed credit spread is not only EL; it can embed premia and technicals
FI-156.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。

FI-157.reasoning: Reasoning: POD is driven by profitability, coverage, and leverage (high profit and coverage, low leverage: better). LGD differs by seniority, subordination, and source of repayment — that is why issue ratings are notched even when POD is the same.

why_wrong.B: Senior unsecured recovery is not 100%; LGD is why notching exists.
why_wrong.C: An issuer rating exists precisely as a family-level POD/creditworthiness view; issues are then notched.

FI-157.zh: 同一發行人違約機率可以一樣，但損失率因順位、次順位、還款來源而不同，所 以單張券評等會notch。不是senior unsecured 回收一定100%。
FI-157.core_idea: POD is driven by profitability, coverage, and leverage; LGD differs by seniority
FI-157.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。

FI-158.reasoning: Reasoning: Corporate ratio core: profitability (EBIT margin), coverage (EBIT / interest), leverage (debt / EBITDA, retained cash flow / net debt). Higher coverage and lower leverage support better credit. Collateral matters more as quality falls.

why_wrong.B: Weaker profitability and higher leverage worsen credit.
why_wrong.C: Collateral: identifiable saleable assets (patents) count; goodwill does not. More goodwill is not the credit-supportive collateral move.

FI-158.zh: 覆蓋率上升、槓桿下降，信用比較好。EBIT 利率倍數變高、debt/EBITDA 變 低。商譽不算可辨認可出售擔保。
FI-158.core_idea: Higher coverage and lower leverage support better credit
FI-158.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。

FI-159.reasoning: Reasoning: Local-currency ratings are typically stronger than foreign-currency ratings: the sovereign can print the former. A domestic currency that is a reserve currency is a credit strength. Qualitative factors include institutions, fiscal flexibility, monetary credibility, diversification, and external / reserve-currency status.

why_wrong.B: The chapter does not rank local-currency as structurally subordinated; it ranks it typically stronger.
why_wrong.C: Sovereign analysis is ability and willingness to pay; ratings can differ by currency.

FI-159.zh: 本幣評等通常優於外幣，因為主權可以印本幣。本幣若還是準備貨幣，更是加分。 不是本幣債結構性次於外幣債。
FI-159.core_idea: Sovereign local-currency ratings are typically stronger than foreign-currency ratings
FI-159.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。

FI-160.reasoning: Reasoning: Yield spread = credit spread + liquidity spread, after stripping the benchmark. Distressed pricing focuses on default timing and expected recovery.

why_wrong.A: Credit-spread risk is the risk that expected loss worsens because credit conditions change — not a pure benchmark-yield move.
why_wrong.C: Rating outlooks track market conditions more closely than the ratings themselves; prices and spreads usually move before the rating — the opposite of “ratings always first.”

FI-160.zh: 扣掉基準之後，殖利率利差＝信用利差＋流動性利差。價格與利差通常走在評等 前面。信用利差風險是預期損失變差，不是公債殖利率自己在動。
FI-160.core_idea: Yield spread = credit spread + liquidity spread after stripping the benchmark; prices often move before the rating
FI-160.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。

FI-161.reasoning: Reasoning: Originator / seller transfers a pool to an SPE. The SPE issues ABS. A trustee holds the assets. Benefits include cheaper funding, a stronger legal claim than a general bank deposit, more origination capacity, and a risk/return slice investors can actually buy.

why_wrong.B: The trustee holds the assets; dual recourse is the covered-bond holder, not the ABS trustee as residual equity.
why_wrong.C: A benefit is a stronger legal claim to the pool than a general bank deposit, not the same claim.

FI-161.zh: SPE 破產隔離：發起人倒了，不一定拖垮ABS。投資人買的是資產池切出來的風 險／報酬層。不要把SPE 當成普通存款，也不要把受託人當成剩餘權益＋雙追索。
FI-161.core_idea: The SPE is bankruptcy remote: the seller’s bankruptcy need not impair the ABS
FI-161.study_section: Securitization and Tranches ｜證券化與分層
FI-161.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。
FI-161.subtopic: 7.6 Securitization and Tranches ｜證券化與分層

FI-162.reasoning: Reasoning: Senior takes contractual cash first and losses last; mezzanine sits in the middle; equity / residual takes remaining cash last and losses first, and is the marginal price-setting investor. Time tranching is speed of principal; credit tranching is who is hurt first.

why_wrong.A: The definitions are swapped; IO/PO are not the chapter’s definition of credit tranching.
why_wrong.B: Junior-first losses is not the same as junior-first prepayments. The two waterfalls are distinct.

FI-162.zh: 信用分層：誰先虧。時間分層：本金回來的快慢（提前還款風險）。Junior 先虧̸= junior 先拿到提前還款。
FI-162.core_idea: Credit tranching: who takes losses first; time tranching: how fast principal returns
FI-162.study_section: Securitization and Tranches ｜證券化與分層
FI-162.exam_trap: Confusing who takes losses first with who receives prepayments first
FI-162.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。
FI-162.subtopic: 7.6 Securitization and Tranches ｜證券化與分層

FI-163.reasoning: Reasoning: Credit-loss priority: juniors absorb losses before seniors. Principal / prepayment waterfall: sequential-pay principal usually retires the senior sequential class first. That is not the same waterfall.

why_wrong.A: Sequential-pay is not defined as pro-rata sharing of both waterfalls.
why_wrong.C: “Junior” is first-loss, last residual cash — not first prepayments. Sequential principal retires the senior sequential class first.

FI-163.zh: 兩條瀑布：虧錢junior 先頂；本金／提前還款先還指定的先前／優先sequential 層。不要把「次順位」讀成「先拿提前還款」。
FI-163.core_idea: Sequential-pay: juniors absorb credit losses first; principal/prepayments retire the senior sequential class first
FI-163.study_section: Sequential-Pay CMBS and Time Tranching ｜CMBS 順序分層與時間分層
FI-163.exam_trap: Confusing who takes losses first with who receives prepayments first
FI-163.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。
FI-163.subtopic: 7.6 Sequential-Pay CMBS and Time Tranching ｜CMBS 順序分層與時間分層

FI-164.reasoning: Reasoning: Principal collections and prepayments generally pay the designated earlier / senior sequential class first until that class is retired, then move to the next class. Credit losses still hit juniors first. Do not treat a prepayment as a default loss.

why_wrong.B: Prepayment is return of principal, not a credit loss. Seniors taking principal first is not seniors taking losses first.
why_wrong.C: Equity / residual is last cash, first loss — the opposite of first claim on prepay principal.

FI-164.zh: 提前還款是本金回來，先還senior sequential，不是先記一筆senior 信用損失。權 益層是最後拿剩餘、最先承受損失，不是先拿提前還款。
FI-164.core_idea: A prepayment that retires the senior sequential class does not mean seniors take losses first
FI-164.study_section: Sequential-Pay CMBS and Time Tranching ｜CMBS 順序分層與時間分層
FI-164.exam_trap: Confusing who takes losses first with who receives prepayments first
FI-164.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。
FI-164.subtopic: 7.6 Sequential-Pay CMBS and Time Tranching ｜CMBS 順序分層與時間分層

FI-165.reasoning: Reasoning: Credit-loss priority and the principal / prepayment waterfall are two different waterfalls. Juniors take losses first even if they are last in line for scheduled and prepaid principal.

why_wrong.B: CMBS sequential-pay uses juniors to absorb credit losses; IO/PO are a different CMO tool.
why_wrong.C: The senior sequential class is first for principal, not first for losses. Using the principal waterfall to allocate losses is the trap.

FI-165.zh: 違約損失仍是junior 先吸收，即使他們還沒輪到拿sequential 本金。不要因為 senior 先拿本金，就讓senior 先認列信用損失。
FI-165.core_idea: Junior-first losses ̸= junior-first prepayments — reverse scenario
FI-165.study_section: Sequential-Pay CMBS and Time Tranching ｜CMBS 順序分層與時間分層
FI-165.exam_trap: Confusing who takes losses first with who receives prepayments first
FI-165.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。
FI-165.subtopic: 7.6 Sequential-Pay CMBS and Time Tranching ｜CMBS 順序分層與時間分層

FI-166.reasoning: Reasoning: Prepayment risk = contraction + extension. Time tranching redistributes that risk. Credit tranching still decides who is hurt by defaults. Do not infer loss priority from the prepay schedule.

why_wrong.A: A PAC is a scheduled cash-flow class, not automatically first-loss equity. The support tranche absorbs prepayment variation inside a PSA collar.
why_wrong.B: Receiving (or absorbing) prepayment variation is not the credit-loss ranking. The chapter separates time tranching from credit tranching.

FI-166.zh: PAC ／支持層切的是提前還款變異（縮短／延長風險），不是自動改寫誰先承受 信用損失。支持層先扛提前還款，不等於它最後才虧、也不等於它先虧。
FI-166.core_idea: Time tranching redistributes contraction and extension risk; it does not reverse credit-loss priority
FI-166.study_section: Sequential-Pay CMBS and Time Tranching ｜CMBS 順序分層與時間分層
FI-166.exam_trap: Confusing who takes losses first with who receives prepayments first
FI-166.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。
FI-166.subtopic: 7.6 Sequential-Pay CMBS and Time Tranching ｜CMBS 順序分層與時間分層

FI-167.reasoning: Reasoning: A covered bond is not a full securitization: the cover pool stays on the issuer’s balance sheet, typically one bond per pool, dual recourse. Eligibility, dynamic replenishment, and overcollateralization keep credit risk and yield below otherwise similar ABS.

why_wrong.B: Off-balance-sheet SPE with recourse stopping at the pool is the securitization / CDO picture, not the covered bond.
why_wrong.C: CLO equity has recourse that stops at the collateral pool; dual recourse is the covered-bond holder.

FI-167.zh: 擔保債券：資產池留在發行人資產負債表，通常一池一券，持有人有雙追索（隔 離池＋機構未設質資產）。真正出表、只追到資產池的是證券化／CDO。
FI-167.core_idea: A covered bond keeps the cover pool on the issuer’s balance sheet and gives dual recourse
FI-167.study_section: Covered bonds, CDOs, and CLOs ｜擔保債券、CDO 與CLO
FI-167.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。
FI-167.subtopic: 7.6 Covered bonds, CDOs, and CLOs ｜擔保債券、CDO 與CLO

FI-168.reasoning: Reasoning: Equity-tranche holders put up the residual capital, take equity-like risk, and are the marginal, price-setting investors. Recourse stops at the collateral pool. In an arbitrage CDO, promised asset yield exceeds promised liability yield; absent default, the excess is the residual’s cash flow.

why_wrong.A: The deal has to offer equity a competitive return or it does not get done; seniors have the promised coupon.
why_wrong.B: First claim plus dual recourse is senior / covered-bond language, not CLO equity.

FI-168.zh: CLO 權益層：出剩餘資本、最先虧、最後拿契約現金、是邊際定價的人。沒有對 經理人的雙追索。交易必須給他們有競爭力的報酬才做得出來。
FI-168.core_idea: CDO/CLO equity is residual, first-loss, and the price-setting tranche
FI-168.study_section: Covered bonds, CDOs, and CLOs ｜擔保債券、CDO 與CLO
FI-168.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。
FI-168.subtopic: 7.6 Covered bonds, CDOs, and CLOs ｜擔保債券、CDO 與CLO

FI-169.reasoning: Reasoning: After the ramp-up, the CLO manager may replace loans that still meet selection criteria. Recourse stops at the collateral pool.

why_wrong.B: Agency RMBS is the federal-agency / GSE guarantee story, not the CBO definition.
why_wrong.C: Covered bonds keep the pool on BS; CLOs are securitization-style pools with recourse to collateral.

FI-169.zh: CDO 是被管理、用槓桿的債務池。CBO 裝債券，CLO 裝貸款（現金流、市值或 CDS 合成）。CLO 不是資產負債表上的covered bond。
FI-169.core_idea: A CDO is a managed, leveraged pool; CLO is loans; CBO is bonds
FI-169.study_section: Covered bonds, CDOs, and CLOs ｜擔保債券、CDO 與CLO
FI-169.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。
FI-169.subtopic: 7.6 Covered bonds, CDOs, and CLOs ｜擔保債券、CDO 與CLO

FI-170.reasoning: Reasoning: Prepayment risk = contraction + extension. Contraction: principal too soon, usually when rates have fallen. Extension: principal too slowly, usually when rates have risen; remaining cash is discounted at a higher rate and stretched over more years.

why_wrong.B: Extension is the rates-up, prepay-slow case.
why_wrong.C: Agency guarantee is credit, not a prepayment lock; pass-throughs still pay prepaid principal.

FI-170.zh: 利率下跌、提前還款加速：縮短期風險。錢太早回來，再投資變便宜，也少了價 格上漲。延長期是利率上升、本金回來太慢。機構擔保不消除提前還款。
FI-170.core_idea: Contraction: principal too soon (rates down); extension: principal too slow (rates up)
FI-170.study_section: Mortgage-backed and other ABS ｜房貸擔保與其他資產證券化
FI-170.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。
FI-170.subtopic: 7.6 Mortgage-backed and other ABS ｜房貸擔保與其他資產證券化

FI-171.reasoning: Reasoning: A CMO resecuritizes pass-throughs. Sequential-pay: principal fills one tranche, then the next. A Z tranche pays nothing until a start date, then principal plus accrued interest; it is last, it frees cash for earlier tranches, and it has no reinvestment risk during the accretion period.

why_wrong.B: IO receives only interest; PO receives only principal. Z is an accrual principal class.
why_wrong.C: Z is last in the sequential principal sense and is not defined as the credit first-loss PAC support.

FI-171.zh: Z（應計）層：開始日前不配，之後本金加應計利息；排最後，把現金讓給前面的 層，累計期間沒有再投資風險。它不是IO，也不是自動的信用優先虧損層。
FI-171.core_idea: A Z (accrual) tranche pays nothing until a start date, then principal plus accrued interest
FI-171.study_section: Mortgage-backed and other ABS ｜房貸擔保與其他資產證券化
FI-171.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。
FI-171.subtopic: 7.6 Mortgage-backed and other ABS ｜房貸擔保與其他資產證券化

FI-172.reasoning: Reasoning: PO receives only principal and rises when rates fall and prepayments accelerate; IO receives only interest.

why_wrong.B: IO/PO are not defined as PAC scheduled classes.
why_wrong.C: PO is principal-only, not interest-only. It benefits when principal is pulled forward.

FI-172.zh: 利率下跌、提前還款加速：PO（只拿本金）升值；IO（只拿利息）受傷。不要把 PO 當成IO。
FI-172.core_idea: PO rises when rates fall and prepayments accelerate; IO receives only interest
FI-172.study_section: Mortgage-backed and other ABS ｜房貸擔保與其他資產證券化
FI-172.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。
FI-172.subtopic: 7.6 Mortgage-backed and other ABS ｜房貸擔保與其他資產證券化

FI-173.reasoning: Reasoning: CMBS: few commercial mortgages, typically non-recourse, often balloon. Credit screens are LTV and DSCR = NOI / debt service. Balloon risk — failure to refinance the balloon — is a form of extension risk.

why_wrong.A: The pass-through rate is below WAC by the servicing / SPE fee, with WAC = Σ(i×CB)/ΣCB — a different object.
why_wrong.C: Depreciation and P&I are specifically not in this NOI.

FI-173.zh: NOI ＝租金-付現營運費用-重置準備，不含折舊，也不含本金利息。DSCR ＝ NOI ／債務服務。轉付利率低於WAC，是另一件事。
FI-173.core_idea: CMBS credit screens are LTV and DSCR = NOI / debt service; NOI excludes depreciation and P&I
FI-173.study_section: Mortgage-backed and other ABS ｜房貸擔保與其他資產證券化
FI-173.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。
FI-173.subtopic: 7.6 Mortgage-backed and other ABS ｜房貸擔保與其他資產證券化

FI-174.reasoning: Reasoning: Credit-card ABS are non-amortizing. During lockout / revolving, principal collections buy new receivables, so there is no prepayment risk in that window. A rapid-amortization trigger can force early principal return. The structure is not a covered bond.

why_wrong.A: Covered-bond dual recourse is not the credit-card ABS lockout design.
why_wrong.C: Lockout means principal is reinvested in new receivables, not passed through — the opposite of maximized contraction.

FI-174.zh: 信用卡ABS 鎖定期／循環期：收回的本金拿去買新應收帳款，這段沒有提前還款 風險。快速攤還觸發才會提早還本。不是covered bond。
FI-174.core_idea: Credit-card ABS: lockout / revolving period has no prepayment risk in that window
FI-174.study_section: Mortgage-backed and other ABS ｜房貸擔保與其他資產證券化
FI-174.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。
FI-174.subtopic: 7.6 Mortgage-backed and other ABS ｜房貸擔保與其他資產證券化

FI-175.reasoning: Reasoning: Agency RMBS has a federal-agency (full faith) or GSE guarantee; non-agency is private with no such guarantee. Foreclosure lets the lender seize and sell the property. Lower LTV and lower DTI reduce default odds. Prime: low LTV and DTI; subprime is the opposite.

why_wrong.B: Foreclosure lets the lender seize and sell the property; LTV matters.
why_wrong.C: Prime: low LTV and DTI; subprime: the opposite. That choice reversed the labels.

FI-175.zh: 機構RMBS 有聯邦／GSE 保證；非機構沒有。LTV 低、DTI 低，違約機率較 低。Prime 是低LTV ／DTI。法拍是債權人可以扣押變賣。
FI-175.core_idea: Agency versus non-agency RMBS; lower LTV and DTI reduce default odds
FI-175.study_section: Mortgage-backed and other ABS ｜房貸擔保與其他資產證券化
FI-175.source_note: 解答依據 FI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Fixed Income。
FI-175.subtopic: 7.6 Mortgage-backed and other ABS ｜房貸擔保與其他資產證券化

DER-001.reasoning: Reasoning: The chapter’s opening definition: a derivative transforms the performance of an underlying. It does not simply pass the underlying’s return through. The contract can stand alone or be embedded (callable or putable bond). Typical forward commitments are priced so each side has zero value at initiation.

why_wrong.B: Forward commitments are typically set with zero value at initiation and no upfront premium.
why_wrong.C: A callable or putable bond embeds a derivative; the contract need not stand alone.

DER-001.zh: 衍生性商品是「轉換」標的表現，不是把報酬原封不動轉給對手。它可以獨立存 在，也可以嵌在可贖回／可賣回債券裡。遠期承諾型契約成交時價值通常為零，不必先付權利 金。
DER-001.core_idea: A derivative transforms the underlying’s performance; it does not simply pass the return through
DER-001.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-001.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-001.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-002.reasoning: Reasoning: Forward commitments — forwards, futures, and swaps — are binding promises to transact. Contingent claims — options and credit derivatives such as a CDS — pay only if a specified event occurs. One side of an option decides whether to exercise.

why_wrong.A: An embedded call and a credit-spread option are contingent claims, not binding promises to transact.
why_wrong.C: Puts and CDS are contingent claims: they pay only if a specified event (exercise or credit event) occurs.

DER-002.zh: 遠期、期貨、swap 是綁定承諾。選擇權與CDS 是或有請求權，事件沒發生就不 付。不要把「有標的」當成一定是遠期承諾。
DER-002.core_idea: A forward commitment is a binding promise; a contingent claim pays only if a specified event occurs
DER-002.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-002.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-002.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-003.reasoning: Reasoning: An option gives the owner the right, not the obligation, to buy (call) or sell (put). The buyer pays a premium. The seller (writer) receives that premium and has the obligation if the buyer exercises. A long call therefore faces counterparty credit risk on the writer. Only the short can default.

why_wrong.B: The long call faces the writer’s default; cash settlement does not erase that credit exposure.
why_wrong.C: Both sides must transact is the firm-commitment (forward) rule, not the option rule.

DER-003.zh: 選擇權是一方決定行不行權；賣方只有在對方行權時才有義務。遠期是雙方都必 須履約。Long call 仍面對賣方違約風險。
DER-003.core_idea: One side of an option decides whether to exercise; the writer is obligated if the buyer exercises
DER-003.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-003.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-003.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-004.reasoning: Reasoning: Both a forward and a futures set a price today, F0(T), for purchase or sale at date T. The buyer is long: later purchase. The seller is short: later sale. Contract prices are set so each side has zero value at initiation; typically neither party pays an upfront premium. Distinguish that contracted price from later mark-to-market value.

why_wrong.A: A forward is a firm commitment, not a pair of calls. There is one long and one short.
why_wrong.C: The long is the later purchase, not the later sale. The contracted price is not an upfront premium.

DER-004.zh: Long 是以後買、short 是以後賣。成交價F0 訂成雙方期初價值為零，通常沒有先 付的權利金。成交價不是後來的MTM 價值。
DER-004.core_idea: The long later purchases; the short later sells; F0(T) is set so value is zero at initiation
DER-004.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-004.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-004.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-005.reasoning: Reasoning: A deliverable contract is settled by delivery of the asset. A cash-settled contract pays the difference between the contracted price and the spot at settlement. Either form can hedge or speculate. The long’s payoff remains ST - F0(T); only the settlement medium changes.

why_wrong.A: Either form can hedge an existing exposure or speculate on the underlying price.
why_wrong.B: Cash settlement still pays ST - F0(T) to the long (or the reverse to the short). The payoff is not erased.

DER-005.zh: 實物交割是交標的；現金結算是付契約價與即期的差。Long 的到期損益仍是ST - F0。兩種都能避險或投機。
DER-005.core_idea: Deliverable settles by delivery; cash-settled pays the difference between the contracted price and spot
DER-005.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-005.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-005.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-006.reasoning: Reasoning: Speculators use futures to gain exposure to the underlying. Hedgers use them to reduce an exposure they already have. Buying oil futures with no existing oil position is a long speculative exposure, not a hedge.

why_wrong.A: Hedging requires an exposure that is already there. This trader is adding oil risk, not offsetting it.
why_wrong.B: The clearinghouse is the buyer to every seller; a speculative long is not the CCP.

DER-006.zh: 避險是降低「已經有」的曝險。沒有庫存、也沒有預定買賣，只是想賺油價漲，那 是投機做多。
DER-006.core_idea: Hedgers reduce an existing exposure; speculators use the contract to gain exposure
DER-006.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-006.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-006.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-007.reasoning: Reasoning: Credit derivatives are contingent claims on a credit event. A CDS is insurance against default: the protection buyer pays a stream of premiums and receives a payment if the referenced issuer defaults. Credit spread depends on probability of default and loss given default. A creditspread option is typically a call on a bond’s yield spread versus a benchmark.

why_wrong.A: Exchanging fixed for floating with no exchange of notional is a plain vanilla interest-rate swap, a forward commitment.
why_wrong.B: Directional similarity is not payoff identity. A CDS is a credit contingent claim, not a short stock.

DER-007.zh: CDS 是違約保險：買保護的人付權利金，發行人違約才獲賠。它不是利率swap， 也不是放空股票。方向感相似̸= payoff 相同。
DER-007.core_idea: A CDS is insurance against default; a credit-spread option is typically a call on a bond’s yield spread
DER-007.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-007.exam_trap: Equating a credit derivative with a short stock
DER-007.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-007.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-008.reasoning: Reasoning: A credit-spread option is typically a call on a bond’s yield spread versus a benchmark: if credit quality worsens, the spread widens and the option pays. That is a contingent claim on credit, not a stock option and not a required short of the shares.

why_wrong.B: A CDS lets default risk be managed separately from a cash bond; it does not require a short stock.
why_wrong.C: The chapter’s credit-spread option is a call on the yield spread, not an equity call.

DER-008.zh: 信用利差選擇權通常是對利差的call：信用變差、利差變寬才付錢。不要把它當成 股票買權，也不要強迫搭配放空股票。
DER-008.core_idea: A credit-spread option typically pays when the issuer’s yield spread versus a benchmark widens
DER-008.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-008.exam_trap: Reading a credit option as a short stock or equity call
DER-008.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-008.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-009.reasoning: Reasoning: The long forward’s payoff — which is also its value at maturity — is linear in the spot: VT(T) = ST - F0(T) = 80 - 72 = 8. The long gains if ST > F0(T). Distinguish this expiration value from the contracted price 72, which does not reset. A forward typically has no premium, so this payoff is also the long’s profit. Given: Long forward; F0(T) = 72; ST = 80. No premium. Asked: Long payoff (= value at maturity). Formula: VT = 80 −72 Variables: Long = later purchase; short payoff is the negative. Why this formula: The long is obliged to buy at the old contracted price. The difference versus spot is the cash (or delivery) result. The long’s right to buy at 72 is worth 8 when spot is 80. Reasonableness check: Short would be -8. 0 confuses initiation value with maturity value. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。
DER-009.steps: ①Identify the side: long ⇒VT = ST - F0(T). ②80 - 72 = 8. ③Zero at initiation is not zero at T.

why_wrong.A: Value is zero at initiation, not at maturity. At T there is nothing left to discount: VT = ST - F0(T).
why_wrong.C: -8 is the short’s payoff F0(T) - ST, the mirror image.

DER-009.zh: Long 遠期到期損益（也是到期價值）是ST - F0 = 8。Short 才是-8。期初價值為 零，到期不必為零。遠期通常沒權利金，所以這裡payoff 等於profit。
DER-009.core_idea: The long forward’s payoff (and value at maturity) is ST - F0(T)
DER-009.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-009.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-009.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-010.reasoning: Reasoning: The short is the later sale. Payoff = F0(T) - ST = 72 - 80 = -8. Always name the side before writing a sign. Because a standard forward has no premium, this payoff is also the short’s profit. Given: Short forward; F0(T) = 72; ST = 80. Asked: Short payoff. Formula: 72 −80 Variables: Short = later sale. Why this formula: The short must sell at 72 when the asset is worth 80. A later sale at a below-spot contracted price loses 8. Reasonableness check: Do not report the contracted price 72 as a payoff. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。

why_wrong.A: 8 is the long’s payoff. The short is the mirror image.
why_wrong.C: The contracted price is the trade price, not the short’s P&L. Payoff is F0 - ST.

DER-010.zh: Short 是以後賣，損益是F0 - ST = -8。先寫部位再寫正負。遠期沒權利金，payoff 就是profit。
DER-010.core_idea: The short forward’s payoff is F0(T) - ST, the mirror image of the long
DER-010.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-010.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-010.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-011.reasoning: Reasoning: Long payoff VT = ST - F0(T) = 49 - 55 = -6. The long gains only if ST > F0(T). The contracted price stayed 55; it is not marked to the new spot except through this difference. No premium, so profit equals this payoff. Given: Long; F0 = 55; ST = 49. Asked: Long payoff (= profit, no premium). Formula: 49 −55 Variables: Distinguish payoff from the contracted price and from the spot level. Why this formula: Linear firm commitment: the signed gap versus F0. Buying at an above-spot forward price loses. Reasonableness check: Sign flips if the side is misread as short. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。

why_wrong.B: Payoff is ST - F0, not the spot level itself.
why_wrong.C: 6 would be the short’s payoff, or a sign error on the long.

DER-011.zh: Long 用55 買進現貨只值49，payoff = -6。不要把short 的+6 或即期49 當成答 案。
DER-011.core_idea: The long loses when ST is below the contracted forward price
DER-011.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-011.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-011.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-012.reasoning: Reasoning: Because the payoff is a straight line through the underlying, firm commitments are linear derivatives. The long cannot discard a negative VT. That is why a long forward can be negative at T, while a long call struck at the same F0(T) floors the same comparison at zero.

why_wrong.A: Forwards typically have no daily margin. Linearity is the payoff shape, not a futures-margin story.
why_wrong.B: Walking away is an option. A forward is a binding promise; the long must absorb ST < F0.

DER-012.zh: 遠期是直線：漲也跟、跌也跟，沒有歸零下限。不能像call 一樣放棄。這叫線性 衍生工具。
DER-012.core_idea: Firm commitments are linear derivatives: payoff is a straight line through the underlying
DER-012.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-012.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-012.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-013.reasoning: Reasoning: If the expected future price rises during the life, the right to buy at the original forward price has positive value and the obligation to sell has equal negative value. The contracted price F0(T) is unchanged; mark-to-market value moves. That is the price-versus-value distinction.

why_wrong.A: The long, not the short, owns the cheap purchase right when the expected future price has risen.
why_wrong.B: F0(T) stays fixed, but value is the gap versus the new market. Price ̸= value.

DER-013.zh: 成交價F0 不變，但價值會變。預期未來價漲，long 的「用舊價買」變值錢，short 等額虧。不要把「價格固定」說成「價值永遠是零」。
DER-013.core_idea: If the expected future price rises, the long’s right to buy at the old F0 has positive value
DER-013.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-013.exam_trap: Treating a fixed contracted price as zero value after initiation
DER-013.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-013.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-014.reasoning: Reasoning: If the expected future price falls below the contracted forward price, the short’s right to sell at an above-market price is the side that is worth something. The long is the equal negative. Name the side; do not assume the long cannot lose.

why_wrong.B: Value moves as soon as the market diverges from F0; it does not wait until T.
why_wrong.C: A long forward is not a call; it can be negative. The cheap purchase right is not the valuable side here.

DER-014.zh: 預期未來價跌破舊F0，有價值的是short（能用偏高契約價賣出）。Long 遠期可 以是負值，不是call。
DER-014.core_idea: If the expected future price falls below F0(T), the short’s right to sell at an above-market price has value
DER-014.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-014.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-014.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-015.reasoning: Reasoning: Forwards are customized OTC contracts. They are less transparent and less liquid than exchange-traded contracts, and each side faces the other as counterparty. Futures are standardized, exchange-traded, and backed by a clearinghouse. OTC ̸= unregulated as a definition.

why_wrong.B: Standardization, novation, and easy offset describe futures, not forwards.
why_wrong.C: The chapter is explicit: OTC is not a synonym for unregulated. Forwards usually are not regulated the way futures markets are, but that is not an identity.

DER-015.zh: 遠期是店頭、客製、雙方面對面。期貨才是標準化、交易所、結算所承接下來。 OTC 不是「不受監管」的同義詞。
DER-015.core_idea: Forwards are customized OTC contracts; each side faces the other as counterparty
DER-015.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-015.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-015.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-016.reasoning: Reasoning: Payoff is the exercise-or-settlement result: ST - F0 = 5 for the long. Profit subtracts a premium the long paid. A standard forward has no premium, so payoff equals profit. That is the opposite of the option trap, where payoff and profit differ by c0 or p0. Given: Long forward; F0 = 41; ST = 46; no premium. Asked: Payoff and profit. Formula: 46 −41 Variables: Payoff vs profit coincide when the premium is zero. Why this formula: Profit = payoff - premium paid. Premium = 0. Name payoff versus profit; here they match. Reasonableness check: Options would subtract a premium. Forwards typically do not. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。

why_wrong.A: Payoff is ST - F0 = 5, not the spot 46. Do not import the option habit of treating the level as the payoff.
why_wrong.B: There is no “zero-profit convention” that wipes a 5 gap. Daily MTM is a futures story and still accumulates to the same gap.

DER-016.zh: 遠期通常沒權利金，所以到期payoff 等於profit，都是46-41=5。選擇權才要再減 權利金。不要把即期46 當成payoff。
DER-016.core_idea: A standard forward has no premium, so expiration payoff equals profit 核心觀念｜中文理解：遠期通常沒權利金，所以到期payoff 等於profit，都是46-41=5。
DER-016.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-016.exam_trap: Importing the option premium adjustment onto a forward, or treating spot as payoff
DER-016.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-016.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-017.reasoning: Reasoning: If the strike equals the forward price, a long forward’s terminal value is ST - F0(T), which can be negative. A call struck at that same F0(T) floors the same comparison at zero: it is the right, not the obligation, to buy. Do not replace the forward with a call, and do not replace a put with a short stock.

why_wrong.A: The forward does not expire at zero just because it was struck at the original F0. VT = ST - F0 < 0.
why_wrong.C: A call is the right, not the obligation, to buy. It is not a forward. Directional similarity is not payoff identity.

DER-017.zh: 同一價位：遠期會負、call 最多歸零。Call 是權利不是義務，所以不是遠期。方向 感相似̸= payoff 相同。
DER-017.core_idea: A call struck at F0(T) floors the same ST - F0 comparison at zero; a long forward does not
DER-017.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-017.exam_trap: Treating a call struck at the forward as a forward (or a put as short stock)
DER-017.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-017.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-018.reasoning: Reasoning: Futures are standardized, exchange-traded, and backed by a clearinghouse. The clearinghouse is the buyer to every seller and the seller to every buyer, so either side can reverse the position without finding the original counterparty. That novation removes bilateral default exposure from the futures trade.

why_wrong.B: Remaining facing the original name is the forward / uncleared OTC story, not cleared futures.
why_wrong.C: Price-limit rules bound the trade band; they do not novate the contract.

DER-018.zh: 期貨成交後，對手變成結算所：對每個賣方它是買方，對每個買方它是賣方。要 平倉不必找回原來的人。這叫契約更替。
DER-018.core_idea: The clearinghouse is the buyer to every seller and the seller to every buyer (novation)
DER-018.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-018.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-018.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-019.reasoning: Reasoning: Exchange-traded derivatives require central clearing: verification, payment exchange, participant recording, MTM, and collateral at inception. Interest-rate swaps that clear follow the same idea: executed on a SEF, shared with a CCP, and the CCP replaces both original names. Each intermediary then faces the CCP, not the other dealer.

why_wrong.B: Clearing does not turn the swap into an option. It replaces names; it does not create a put.
why_wrong.C: The chapter states that interest-rate swaps that clear follow the futures idea: SEF, share with a CCP, novation.

DER-019.zh: 會清算的利率swap，概念和期貨一樣：成交後CCP 承接雙方，你面對的是CCP， 不是原來的交易商。這不是變成put。
DER-019.core_idea: Interest-rate swaps that clear follow the same novation idea through a CCP
DER-019.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-019.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-019.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-020.reasoning: Reasoning: Both the long and the short deposit initial margin before the trade — a performance guarantee, not a payment for the contract. Distinguish that collateral from the contracted futures price and from an option premium. Daily MTM then credits or debits the account; variation margin settles the difference.

why_wrong.A: Both sides post initial margin. It is not an option premium and not paid by the long only.
why_wrong.B: F0(T) is the contracted futures price, not cash paid for the asset at initiation. Price ̸= a day-one invoice for the underlying.

DER-020.zh: 初始保證金是履約擔保，多空都要放，不是買合約的價款，也不是選擇權權利金。 F0 是契約價格，不是第一天就把標的買下來。
DER-020.core_idea: Initial margin is a performance guarantee, not a payment for the contract
DER-020.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-020.exam_trap: Reading initial margin as the purchase price or as an option premium
DER-020.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-020.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-021.reasoning: Reasoning: MTM gain/loss = [F1(T) - F0(T)] × n = (1,827 - 1,820) × 250 = 1,750 for the long. The short is the mirror image: a 1,750 loss. The margin balance is yesterday’s balance plus that day’s gain. This is realized variation; it is not the contracted price changing into a new “value” that remains open — daily settlement resets the remaining futures value to zero. Given: Long; F_open = 1,820; F_close = 1,827; n = 250. Asked: That day’s MTM for the long. Formula: (1827 −1820) × 250 Variables: n is contract size. Long gains when F1 > F0. Why this formula: Daily settlement recognizes the change in the futures price times size. The long is marked in when the futures price rises. Reasonableness check: Short would lose 1,750. Ignoring n leaves 7. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。
DER-021.steps: ①Identify long. ②Price change = 7. ③7 × 250 = 1,750 gain.

why_wrong.A: MTM = (F1 - F0) × n = 7 × 250 = 1,750, not the raw 7-point move.
why_wrong.C: The price rose, so the long gains. A loss would be the short’s result, or a sign flip.

DER-021.zh: Long 的當日MTM = (今收- 今開) × 契約規模= 7 × 250 = 1,750（獲利）。Short 是-1,750。不要只報7 點、也不要看反多空。
DER-021.core_idea: Daily MTM gain/loss is [F1(T) - F0(T)] × n
DER-021.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-021.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-021.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-022.reasoning: Reasoning: Price decline of 1.30 × 1,000 = 1,300. The long’s MTM is -1,300; the short’s MTM is +1,300. Variation margin is exchanged to settle the difference. Name the side before attaching the sign. Cumulative realized MTM over the life is comparable to the payoff on the matching forward. Given: Short; open 98.50; close 97.20; n = 1,000. Asked: Short’s same-day MTM. Formula: (98.50 −97.20) × 1000 Variables: Short gains when the futures price falls. Why this formula: Mirror image of the long’s [F1 - F0] × n. A later seller is marked in when the quoted futures price drops. Reasonableness check: Do not zero out the cash transfer. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。
DER-022.steps: ①Side = short. ②F fell by 1.30. ③1.30 × 1,000 = 1,300 gain.

why_wrong.A: Daily settlement resets the remaining contract value to zero after the day’s gain or loss is paid. It does not erase that day’s cash P&L.
why_wrong.C: The futures price fell. The short (later seller) gains: (98.50 - 97.20) × 1,000 = 1,300. A loss is the long’s result.

DER-022.zh: 期貨價跌，short 才賺：(98.50-97.20)×1,000 = 1,300。Long 是虧1,300。每日結算 是把「剩下的合約價值」歸零，不是把當天已實現損益抹掉。
DER-022.core_idea: A fall in the futures price is an MTM loss for the long and a gain for the short
DER-022.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-022.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-022.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-023.reasoning: Reasoning: Each day the account is marked to market. Variation margin is exchanged to settle the difference. Daily settlement resets the futures contract’s mark-to-market value to zero. The contracted futures price for the next day is the new market price. Distinguish that resetting of remaining value from the cash that already moved.

why_wrong.A: Variation margin is not an option premium. Both sides already posted initial margin as a guarantee.
why_wrong.C: F0 on day one is the contracted price, not a prepaid asset that remains after MTM. Price ̸= leftover value.

DER-023.zh: 變動保證金把當天差額結清後，期貨「剩下的」MTM 價值歸零。這不是把F0 變 成預付資產，也不是選擇權權利金。
DER-023.core_idea: Variation margin is exchanged to settle the day’s difference; remaining futures value resets to zero
DER-023.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-023.exam_trap: Confusing remaining futures value with the contracted price or with a premium
DER-023.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-023.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-024.reasoning: Reasoning: Open interest is the number of outstanding contracts of a given type. It rises when traders open new paired long and short positions and falls when they close existing ones. It is not the settlement price and not that day’s MTM cash.

why_wrong.A: A long closing opposite a short who is also closing reduces open interest.
why_wrong.C: Open interest is the number of outstanding contracts, not the settlement price or the day’s MTM.

DER-024.zh: 未平倉量是還在場上的契約對數。新增多空配對才會升；兩邊都平倉會降。它不 是結算價，也不是當天MTM。
DER-024.core_idea: Open interest rises when traders open new paired longs and shorts and falls when they close existing ones
DER-024.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-024.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-024.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-025.reasoning: Reasoning: The settlement price is an average of prices during the closing period, set by the exchange, and is the basis for the day’s MTM. On the final trading day it equals the spot of the underlying. That last equality is why a maturing futures converges to cash.

why_wrong.A: A futures price moves every day. Treating F0 as frozen is the forward story.
why_wrong.C: MTM uses the closing-period settlement, not the open print as a day-long freeze.

DER-025.zh: 結算價是收盤時段的平均，由交易所訂，用來做當天MTM。最後交易日它等於現 貨。不要把它和開盤第一筆或舊的F0 搞混。
DER-025.core_idea: The settlement price is an average of prices in the closing period and is the basis for that day’s MTM
DER-025.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-025.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-025.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-026.reasoning: Reasoning: A price limit is a band around the previous day’s settlement inside which trades must occur. Trading outside the band requires both parties’ agreement, or the exchange may impose a circuit breaker that pauses intraday trading for a brief period if a limit is reached.

why_wrong.B: Initial margin is a performance guarantee, not the definition of the limit band.
why_wrong.C: A price limit does not floor the long like a put. Linearity of the commitment is unchanged when trading resumes.

DER-026.zh: 漲跌停是上一交易日結算價附近的交易區間。超出要雙方同意，或交易所可能熔 斷暫停。它不會把期貨變成put。
DER-026.core_idea: A price limit is a band around the previous settlement; a circuit breaker can pause trading if a limit is reached
DER-026.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-026.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-026.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-027.reasoning: Reasoning: A forward’s contracted price F0(T) stays fixed until maturity. There is typically no margin deposit. Value is the difference between the current spot and the present value of that contracted price, and settlement waits until T. A futures price moves every day; daily settlement recognizes realized MTM; remaining value resets to zero.

why_wrong.A: Daily reset of remaining value to zero is the futures / daily-settlement story, not the forward story.
why_wrong.B: Forwards typically have no margin deposit. Credit risk remains because settlement waits until T.

DER-027.zh: 遠期：成交價鎖死、通常無保證金、價值= 現貨相對契約價現值的差、到期才結 算，所以有對手信用風險。期貨：每天結算、剩餘價值歸零。
DER-027.core_idea: A forward’s F0(T) stays fixed until maturity; value is the gap versus the PV of that contracted price
DER-027.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-027.exam_trap: Applying daily futures reset to a forward’s contracted price
DER-027.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-027.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-028.reasoning: Reasoning: When the futures is short-dated and parties can borrow at the risk-free rate, futures and forward prices have no material distinction, with two qualifications. Interest-rate contracts: forwards have a convex (nonlinear) price–yield relationship; interest-rate futures are treated as linear in yield. That convexity bias can separate the two prices.

why_wrong.A: Interest-rate futures exist; the chapter discusses their linear-in-yield treatment versus convex forwards.
why_wrong.B: A standard forward has no option premium. That is a different contract family.

DER-028.zh: 利率遠期對殖利率是凸性（非線性）；利率期貨被當成對殖利率線性。這個凸性偏 誤可以讓兩個價格分開。不是因為遠期付了權利金。
DER-028.core_idea: Interest-rate forwards are convex in yield; interest-rate futures are treated as linear — convexity bias 核心觀念｜中文理解：利率遠期對殖利率是凸性（非線性）；利率期貨被當成對殖利率線性。
DER-028.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-028.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-028.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-029.reasoning: Reasoning: If the underlying is positively correlated with rates, a long futures position tends to receive cash when rates are high and to pay cash when rates are low — a net benefit — so futures prices lie above forward prices. Negative correlation reverses the inequality. If rates are uncorrelated with futures prices, or rates are constant, the prices coincide.

why_wrong.A: Positive correlation is a net benefit to the long futures, which cheapens the futures relative to the benefit — i.e. the futures price is set higher. The opposite inequality is the negative-correlation case.
why_wrong.C: The chapter is explicit: uncorrelated or constant rates make the prices coincide; nonzero correlation can separate them.

DER-029.zh: 標的與利率正相關：期貨多方常常在利率高時收到現金、利率低時付出現金，有 淨好處，所以期貨價格會高於遠期。負相關則相反。
DER-029.core_idea: If the underlying is positively correlated with rates, futures prices lie above forward prices 核心觀念｜中文理解：標的與利率正相關：期貨多方常常在利率高時收到現金、利率低時付出現金，有淨好 處，所以期貨價格會高於遠期。
DER-029.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-029.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-029.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-030.reasoning: Reasoning: Negative correlation reverses the positive-correlation result: the long futures tends to receive cash when rates are low and pay when rates are high — a net cost — so futures prices lie below forward prices. Always separate the contracted price comparison from each contract’s value path.

why_wrong.B: Zero correlation (or constant rates) makes the prices coincide, not a permanent futures discount.
why_wrong.C: Positive correlation is the case in which futures prices lie above forwards.

DER-030.zh: 標的與利率負相關時，期貨多方的每日結算比較吃虧，期貨價格會低於遠期。正 相關才是期貨價較高。零相關則兩者重合。
DER-030.core_idea: Negative correlation of the underlying with rates puts futures prices below forward prices 核心觀念｜中文理解：標的與利率負相關時，期貨多方的每日結算比較吃虧，期貨價格會低於遠期。
DER-030.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-030.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-030.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-031.reasoning: Reasoning: Hedgers go short the derivative when that instrument’s financial risk is positively correlated with the risk they already bear. Inventory is a long copper exposure. A fall in the copper price reduces inventory value; a short copper futures gains in that same state and offsets the inventory loss. The test is correlation with the exposure you already have, not whether copper appears in the production process.

why_wrong.B: The chapter’s inventory hedge is a short futures when futures move with the inventory. A long call is a long-volatility overlay, not that hedge.
why_wrong.C: “Uses copper, so buy futures” is the input-purchase instinct. It is the right hedge only if the firm is not yet long copper. Inventory is already a long.

DER-031.zh: 已持有銅庫存= 已經做多銅。銅價跌、庫存跌，對沖必須short 期貨。看到 manufacturer ／要用銅就去long，是同一側加碼，不是避險。
DER-031.core_idea: Hedgers go short the derivative when that instrument is positively correlated with the risk they already bear
DER-031.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-031.exam_trap: Hedging by taking the same side as the business, not the opposite side
DER-031.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-031.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-032.reasoning: Reasoning: Buying copper futures feels like locking in an input — and that is the right hedge if the firm is not yet long copper. The existing exposure is the need to buy later. A rise in copper hurts that plan; a long futures gains in that same state. First ask: am I already long or already short the risk? Then take the opposite side of the derivative.

why_wrong.A: The hedge is in copper, the risk that is correlated with the exposure, not a sale of finished wire.
why_wrong.C: Short futures would add to the “must buy later” risk: if copper rises, the plant pays more cash and the short futures also loses.

DER-032.zh: 還沒有庫存、以後才要買= 現在是空銅。銅價漲會傷進貨成本，對沖是long 期 貨。不要用「工廠都該賣期貨」一刀切。
DER-032.core_idea: If the firm must buy later and does not hold inventory, the copper hedge is long futures
DER-032.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-032.exam_trap: Hedging by taking the same side as the business, not the opposite side
DER-032.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-032.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-033.reasoning: Reasoning: The existing exposure is long wheat (the growing crop). A fall in wheat reduces the value of that crop. Short wheat futures gain in that same state. Do not hear “farmer / producer” and buy futures as if the firm were a later buyer. Opposite side of the exposure you already have.

why_wrong.B: The grower is a later seller, already long the crop. Buying futures would double the long.
why_wrong.C: The chapter’s inventory / producer hedge is short the positively correlated futures. It does not require adding a put-plus-long-futures package.

DER-033.zh: 農夫以後要賣糧= 已經做多農產品。糧價跌傷收成，對沖是short 期貨。不要把 「生產者」聽成「要用這個東西所以該買」。
DER-033.core_idea: A producer who will sell the harvest is already long the crop; the hedge is short futures
DER-033.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-033.exam_trap: Hedging by taking the same side as the business, not the opposite side
DER-033.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-033.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-034.reasoning: Reasoning: Hedgers go short when the instrument is positively correlated with the risk they already bear. If the existing exposure were inversely related to the derivative, the hedge would be long. The test is correlation with the exposure you already have, not a blanket “sell futures.”

why_wrong.A: Long-and-short the same futures is a flat speculation book, not a hedge of an outside exposure.
why_wrong.C: “Hedgers are short” is the positively correlated case (inventory, harvest). Inverse correlation flips the sign.

DER-034.zh: 期貨若與你已有曝險負相關，避險反而是long。只有正相關（庫存、收成）才 short。不要背「避險者一定空」。
DER-034.core_idea: If the existing exposure is inversely related to the derivative, the hedge is long
DER-034.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-034.exam_trap: Hedging by taking the same side as the business, not the opposite side
DER-034.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-034.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-035.reasoning: Reasoning: The existing exposure is the need to buy fuel (short the commodity). A rise in fuel hurts. Long fuel futures gain in that same state. Do not take the same side as “we use fuel.”

why_wrong.A: Equity is not the chapter’s hedge of a commodity purchase. Use the correlated fuel futures, opposite the exposure.
why_wrong.B: Consuming fuel later is a planned purchase. Selling futures would lose when fuel (and the cash bill) rises.

DER-035.zh: 航空公司以後要買油、手上沒庫存= 空油。油價漲會傷，對沖是long 燃油期貨。 不要因為「我們有用油」就去賣期貨。
DER-035.core_idea: An airline that must buy jet fuel later is short the commodity; the hedge is long fuel futures
DER-035.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-035.exam_trap: Hedging by taking the same side as the business, not the opposite side
DER-035.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-035.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-036.reasoning: Reasoning: Inventory is long gold. A price decline hurts inventory and helps a short futures. Opposite side; positive correlation. “We use gold” is not the test.

why_wrong.A: A long call is not the linear short-futures inventory hedge.
why_wrong.C: Using gold in a workshop does not flip an already-long inventory into a short. Same-side long futures adds risk.

DER-036.zh: 已持有黃金庫存就是做多黃金。金價跌傷庫存，對沖short 期貨。不要用「店裡要 做珠寶」當同一側做多的理由。
DER-036.core_idea: A merchant already long bullion hedges with short gold futures
DER-036.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-036.exam_trap: Hedging by taking the same side as the business, not the opposite side
DER-036.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-036.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-037.reasoning: Reasoning: The test is correlation with the exposure you already have, not whether the commodity appears in your production process. A is already long (inventory) →short futures. B is already short the commodity (must buy) →long futures.

why_wrong.A: “Both use copper” ignores the existing-exposure test. B is not yet long copper.
why_wrong.B: A short is correct only for the already-long inventory. B’s planned purchase is the other sign.

DER-037.zh: 先問現在曝險是多還是空，再取相反方向。兩家都「用銅」不代表同一側避險：有 庫存要空、以後才買要多。
DER-037.core_idea: The test is correlation with the exposure you already have, not whether the commodity appears in production
DER-037.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-037.exam_trap: Hedging by taking the same side as the business, not the opposite side
DER-037.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-037.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-038.reasoning: Reasoning: Fair-value hedge: varying fair value of an asset or liability — example, commodity futures on inventory when a lower future price is the concern. That concern is a long inventory; the futures side that gains when the price falls is the short. Cash-flow hedges absorb varying cash flows (pay-fixed swap on floating-rate debt; FX forward on forecasted sales).

why_wrong.B: A currency swap or currency forward on the equity of a foreign operation is the net-investment example.
why_wrong.C: Pay-fixed on floating debt is the cash-flow-hedge example, not inventory.

DER-038.zh: 庫存怕跌價，是公允價值避險，期貨方向是short。不要和浮動負債的現金流避 險、或國外營運淨投資避險搞混。
DER-038.core_idea: A fair-value inventory hedge uses futures when a lower future price is the concern
DER-038.study_section: Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨
DER-038.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-038.subtopic: 8.1 Forwards and Futures ｜遠期契約與期貨

DER-039.reasoning: Reasoning: Long call: right to buy; premium paid; positive delta; wants S up. The long’s loss is limited to the premium paid; the gain on a long call is not bounded. Do not swap this for a short call or for a long put, and do not replace a put with a short stock.

why_wrong.A: Right to sell is a long put. A long put is not a short stock; directional similarity is not payoff identity.
why_wrong.B: Obligation to sell, premium received, negative delta is a short call.

DER-039.zh: Long call：付錢買「用X 買進」的權利，要標的漲，虧最多權利金。不要和short call（收錢、有義務賣）或long put 搞混；long put 也不是放空現貨。
DER-039.core_idea: Long call: right to buy, premium paid, positive delta, wants S up
DER-039.study_section: Option payoffs and time value ｜選擇權到期損益與時間價值
DER-039.exam_trap: Equating long put with short the underlying (or swapping call/put sides)
DER-039.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-039.subtopic: 8.2 Option payoffs and time value ｜選擇權到期損益與時間價值

DER-040.reasoning: Reasoning: Short call: obligation to sell; premium received; negative delta; wants S down. The short receives the premium and bears the obligation. Only the short can default. A long call therefore faces counterparty credit risk on the writer. Do not rewrite the short call as a short stock.

why_wrong.A: A short call has negative delta but is not a short stock. Directional similarity is not payoff identity.
why_wrong.C: The exercise choice belongs to the long. The writer’s loss on a call is not limited to the premium.

DER-040.zh: Short call：收了權利金，對方若行權你必須賣。你要標的跌。只有空方會違約。 負delta 不是放空現貨。
DER-040.core_idea: Short call: obligation to sell, premium received, negative delta, wants S down
DER-040.study_section: Option payoffs and time value ｜選擇權到期損益與時間價值
DER-040.exam_trap: Equating an option with a stock position of the same delta sign
DER-040.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-040.subtopic: 8.2 Option payoffs and time value ｜選擇權到期損益與時間價值

DER-041.reasoning: Reasoning: Long put is the right to sell the underlying to X. You want the underlying down: spot below the strike makes exercise worthwhile. You can lose no more than the premium already paid. Directional similarity ̸= the same payoff: a long put is not a short of the cash asset. The put’s payoff is nonlinear and floored.

why_wrong.A: Negative delta is a directional similarity, not payoff identity. A short stock’s loss is not floored at a premium.
why_wrong.C: The obligation to buy if exercised is a short put, not a long put.

DER-041.zh: Long put 是「有權把標的賣到X」，要標的跌，虧最多已付權利金。方向和放空現 貨相似，但payoff 不同：有下限、非线性。Long put ̸= short 現貨。
DER-041.core_idea: Long put: right to sell at X, premium paid, negative delta, wants S down; loss limited to the premium
DER-041.study_section: Option payoffs and time value ｜選擇權到期損益與時間價值
DER-041.exam_trap: Equating long put with short the underlying
DER-041.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-041.subtopic: 8.2 Option payoffs and time value ｜選擇權到期損益與時間價值

DER-042.reasoning: Reasoning: Short put: you collected the premium; if the other side wants to sell, you must buy. You want the underlying up so the buyer abandons exercise. If the underlying falls sharply, you are forced to take the asset at a rich X. That is the short-put risk. A short put has positive delta, but it is not equivalent to owning the underlying.

why_wrong.B: The right to sell is the long put. The short put is the opposite obligation.
why_wrong.C: Positive delta is not ownership of the underlying. A short put’s loss when S collapses is the forced purchase at a rich X, not a stock’s linear gain profile.

DER-042.zh: Short put：收了權利金，對方要賣你就得買。你要標的漲、對方放棄。大跌時你 被迫用偏高的X 接貨。正delta ̸= 做多現貨。
DER-042.core_idea: Short put: obligation to buy at X, premium received, positive delta, wants S up
DER-042.study_section: Option payoffs and time value ｜選擇權到期損益與時間價值
DER-042.exam_trap: Equating short put with long the underlying
DER-042.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-042.subtopic: 8.2 Option payoffs and time value ｜選擇權到期損益與時間價值

DER-043.reasoning: Reasoning: The long’s loss is limited to the premium paid. The short receives the premium and bears the obligation. Only the short can default. A long call therefore faces counterparty credit risk on the writer. The long option buyer faces the writer’s default — also listed among derivative risks.

why_wrong.A: The chapter: only the short can default. That is why the long faces the writer.
why_wrong.B: Paying a premium does not remove the writer’s later performance risk.

DER-043.zh: 選擇權只有空方會違約。Long call 已付權利金，真正要擔心的是賣方在價內時不 履約。付了權利金̸= 沒有信用風險。
DER-043.core_idea: Only the short can default; a long call faces the writer’s counterparty credit risk
DER-043.study_section: Option payoffs and time value ｜選擇權到期損益與時間價值
DER-043.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-043.subtopic: 8.2 Option payoffs and time value ｜選擇權到期損益與時間價值

DER-044.reasoning: Reasoning: American options may be exercised at any time up to expiration. European options may be exercised only at expiration. That is the only contractual difference. Value differences then follow from whether early exercise can have an advantage (dividends for calls; cash-timing for deep ITM puts).

why_wrong.B: Early exercise is an extra right. It cannot make the American worth less than the European; it can make some Americans worth more.
why_wrong.C: European exercise is only at expiration, not “any date except expiration.”

DER-044.zh: 美式隨時可提前行權，歐式只能到期行權。這是唯一契約差別。提前行權是多出 來的權利，不會讓美式比較便宜。
DER-044.core_idea: American may be exercised any time up to expiration; European only at expiration
DER-044.study_section: Option payoffs and time value ｜選擇權到期損益與時間價值
DER-044.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-044.subtopic: 8.2 Option payoffs and time value ｜選擇權到期損益與時間價值

DER-045.reasoning: Reasoning: A call is more valuable when the issuer of a callable bond wants the right to refinance after rates fall. The call feature is more valuable when the bond’s YTM is below its coupon. A put is the bondholder’s protection: more valuable when YTM exceeds the coupon. Directly, a call’s value rises with time to expiration and with the underlying; it falls when the exercise price rises.

why_wrong.B: A call is the issuer’s right; a put is the holder’s. They are not the same right.
why_wrong.C: YTM above the coupon is the put’s richer region (bondholder protection), not the issuer call.

DER-045.zh: 可贖回債的call 是發行人的：殖利率低於票息、舊票息偏甜、想借新還舊時，call 更值錢。YTM 高於票息才是put（持有人保護）比較值錢。
DER-045.core_idea: A call on a callable bond is more valuable when YTM is below the coupon
DER-045.study_section: Option payoffs and time value ｜選擇權到期損益與時間價值
DER-045.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-045.subtopic: 8.2 Option payoffs and time value ｜選擇權到期損益與時間價值

DER-046.reasoning: Reasoning: A put is the bondholder’s protection: more valuable when YTM exceeds the coupon. Do not swap the call and put regions, and do not treat the put as a short of the issuer’s stock.

why_wrong.A: YTM below coupon enriches the issuer call (refinance). That is the other embedded option.
why_wrong.C: Refinancing after rates fall is the issuer call’s motivation, not the put’s.

DER-046.zh: Put 是持有人的保護：市場殖利率高於票息、債券變便宜時，要求提前還本才值 錢。利率下跌去借新還舊，那是發行人的call。
DER-046.core_idea: A put is the bondholder’s protection and is more valuable when YTM exceeds the coupon
DER-046.study_section: Option payoffs and time value ｜選擇權到期損益與時間價值

DER-047.reasoning: Reasoning: Directly, a call’s value rises with time to expiration and with the underlying; it falls when the exercise price rises. That matches the comparative-static table for European options on assets other than the special put-maturity caveat.

why_wrong.A: A higher X makes the right to buy less valuable, not more.
why_wrong.C: A call wants S up. A falling underlying is the put’s friend.

DER-047.zh: 其他不變：標的漲、到期變長，call 較貴；執行價變高，call 較便宜。不要把call 想成保護性賣權。
DER-047.core_idea: A call’s value rises with time to expiration and with the underlying; it falls when the exercise price rises
