DER-124.reasoning: Reasoning: Interest-rate futures on MRR are often quoted as 100 - (100 × MRR). BPV = notional × 0.01% × period = 1,000,000 × 0.0001 × (90/360) = 25. That is the price change for a one-basispoint change in yield. Given: Notional 1,000,000; period 90/360; one basis point. Asked: BPV. Formula: 1000000 × 0.0001 × (90/360) Variables: 0.01% = 0.0001, not 0.01. Why this formula: One bp of yield on the covered fraction of notional. Each basis point moves this contract $25. Reasonableness check: 100 forgot the quarter. 2,500 used 1%. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。

why_wrong.B: 2,500 is notional × 0.01 × 0.25, using 1% instead of one basis point.
why_wrong.C: 100 is notional × 0.01% with the period dropped (as if the year were the period).

DER-124.core_idea: Interest-rate futures on MRR are often quoted as 100 - (100 × MRR); BPV = notional × 0.01% × period
DER-124.study_section: Interest-rate forwards and swaps ｜利率遠期與交換契約
DER-124.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-124.subtopic: 8.5 Interest-rate forwards and swaps ｜利率遠期與交換契約

DER-125.reasoning: Reasoning: A swap is a firm commitment to exchange a series of payments on periodic settlement dates (the tenor runs to the termination date). On each date the two amounts are netted. A plain vanilla IRS exchanges fixed for floating on a notional that is not itself exchanged. A basis swap exchanges one floating rate for another.

why_wrong.A: Vanilla IRS: notional is not exchanged. There are many settlements, not one FRA.
why_wrong.B: A swap is a forward commitment, not an option. Payments are obligatory.

DER-125.zh: 普通利率交換是綁定承諾：固定對浮動，名目本金不交換，每期淨額交割。它不 是可以放棄的選擇權，也不是單期FRA。
DER-125.core_idea: A swap is a firm commitment to exchange a series of netted payments; a vanilla IRS does not exchange notional
DER-125.study_section: Interest-rate forwards and swaps ｜利率遠期與交換契約
DER-125.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-125.subtopic: 8.5 Interest-rate forwards and swaps ｜利率遠期與交換契約

DER-126.reasoning: Reasoning: The price of the swap is the fixed rate in the contract. That rate is constant. The value of the swap is zero at initiation and then moves as market rates move. The par swap rate is the fixed rate that sets the present value of fixed payments equal to the present value of expected floating payments. It is built from implied forward rates per period (from zero rates), each discounted back on the zero curve.

why_wrong.A: Constant price does not imply constant value. That is the chapter’s price/value mix-up.
why_wrong.B: The contracted fixed rate is not reset to the new par rate. Off-market FRAs inside the swap then have value.

DER-126.zh: Swap 的price 是契約固定利率，成交後不變。Value 期初為零，市場利率一動就 變。不要把「利率沒改」說成「MTM 永遠是零」。
DER-126.core_idea: The price of the swap is the fixed rate (constant); the value is zero at initiation and then moves
DER-126.study_section: Interest-rate forwards and swaps ｜利率遠期與交換契約
DER-126.exam_trap: Treating the constant swap price (fixed rate) as if MTM value could not move
DER-126.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-126.subtopic: 8.5 Interest-rate forwards and swaps ｜利率遠期與交換契約

DER-127.reasoning: Reasoning: Periodic settlement this period is (MRR - sN) × notional × period = (0.042 - 0.036) × 10,000,000 × 0.5 = 30,000 for the pay-fixed / receive-float side. Keep that 30,000 current-period receipt. Whole-swap MTM is the present value of all remaining fixed and floating cash flows, so it depends on the remaining term structure / implied forwards, not on this period’s MRR print alone. Current MRR above 3.60% does not, by itself, prove that the remaining swap has a positive total MTM. The contracted 3.60% is the swap price and is not reset; value is a separate object. Pay-float / receive-fixed — not pay-fixed — has the long fixed-rate-bond profile. Given: Pay-fixed / receive-float; sN = 3.60%; MRR = 4.20%; NP = 10,000,000; period = 0.5. No remaining forward curve is given. Asked: This period net settlement, and whether that print determines remaining-swap MTM Formula: (0.042 −0.036) × 10000000 × 0.5 Variables: sN is the constant swap price. Value is not sN. Why this formula: The floating receipt minus the fixed payment, scaled by notional and the fraction of the year. Keep the 30,000. Do not read the remaining swap total MTM from this period MRR versus 3.60% without the remaining forwards. Reasonableness check: Zero nets would deny the 60 bp gap this period; that still does not price the rest of the tenor. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。
DER-127.steps: ①This period net: (0.042 - 0.036) x 10,000,000 x 0.5 = 30,000 receipt. ②The 30,000 is the current settlement only. ③Remaining-swap MTM is the PV of leftover fixed and floating cash flows; it needs the remaining forward / zero curve. ④Current MRR above 3.60% does not, by itself, prove that the remaining swap has a positive total MTM.
DER-127.final_answer: 30,000 current-period receipt; remaining-swap MTM not determined from this print alone

why_wrong.A: Pay-fixed / receive-float is not the long-bond profile. Pay-float / receive-fixed is. And this period’s cash does not settle the remaining-swap MTM by itself.
why_wrong.B: The 30,000 is this period’s net settlement. Remaining-swap MTM still needs the rest of the forward / zero curve; current MRR above 3.60% is not a whole-swap MTM identity.

DER-127.zh: 本期淨額(4.20%-3.60%)×1,000 萬×0.5=30,000，這筆要留。整段剩餘swap 的 MTM 是剩下固定與浮動現金流的現值，要看剩餘期限結構／遠期利率，不能只因為本期 MRR 高於3.60% 就斷定整段MTM 為正。3.60% 是price，不會被重設。像做多固定利率債 的是pay-float ／收固定，不是pay-fixed。
DER-127.core_idea: Current-period swap settlement is not the remaining-swap MTM; whole-swap value needs the remaining forwards 核心觀念｜中文理解：本期結算30,000 只是這一期淨額；剩餘整段swap 的MTM 還要看剩下的遠期／零 息曲線。
DER-127.study_section: Interest-rate forwards and swaps ｜利率遠期與交換契約
DER-127.exam_trap: Treating this period’s MRR vs fixed as the whole remaining-swap MTM
DER-127.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-127.subtopic: 8.5 Interest-rate forwards and swaps ｜利率遠期與交換契約

DER-128.reasoning: Reasoning: When MRR is above the agreed fixed rate, pay-float / receive-fixed is an MTM loss. A decrease in expected future short-term rates does the opposite: the promised fixed payments are then worth more than the expected floating receipts. Pay-float, receive-fixed has the risk-return profile of a long fixed-rate bond. Price (fixed rate) is unchanged; value moved.

why_wrong.B: Constant price, moving value. The contracted fixed rate does not reset when expected future short-term rates change; the swap’s value does.
why_wrong.C: Receiving the old fixed rate is not a reset to the new higher par rate. The contracted coupon did not rise.

DER-128.zh: Pay-float 收固定：浮動變貴、收到的仍是舊固定，MTM 虧，方向像做多固定利 率債。聽到「收固定」就以為利率升對我有利，是把舊票息聽成已重設。Price 不變̸= value 不變。
DER-128.core_idea: Pay-float / receive-fixed loses when MRR exceeds the agreed fixed rate — same direction as a long fixed-rate bond
DER-128.study_section: Interest-rate forwards and swaps ｜利率遠期與交換契約
DER-128.exam_trap: Swap fixed rate confused with current MTM value — pay-float side
DER-128.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-128.subtopic: 8.5 Interest-rate forwards and swaps ｜利率遠期與交換契約

DER-129.reasoning: Reasoning: Periodic settlement (end of the interest period): (MRR - sN) × notional × period. A swap therefore has many settlements; an FRA has one, and that one is at the start of the period.

why_wrong.A: A swap is a firm commitment, not an option to abandon dates.
why_wrong.C: The chapter contrasts: a swap has many settlements; an FRA has one, and that one is at the start of the period.

DER-129.zh: Swap 有很多期、每期在利息期末淨額交割。FRA 只有一筆，而且在利息期初交 割（還要折現）。Swap 不是可以中途放棄的選擇權。
DER-129.core_idea: A swap has many end-of-period settlements; an FRA has one settlement at the start of its period
DER-129.study_section: Interest-rate forwards and swaps ｜利率遠期與交換契約
DER-129.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-129.subtopic: 8.5 Interest-rate forwards and swaps ｜利率遠期與交換契約

DER-130.reasoning: Reasoning: Those FRAs are generally off-market. Because the swap is worth zero at initiation, the off-market FRA values sum to zero. Issuers can match the cash flows of a balance-sheet liability; investors can change duration and rate exposure without buying or selling the underlying bonds.

why_wrong.A: Daily reset to zero is futures, not a strip of off-market FRAs inside a swap.
why_wrong.B: You do not multiply one MTM by the number of dates. The pieces sum to the swap; at initiation that sum is zero.

DER-130.zh: Swap 的每一期可看成同一契約利率的FRA，但多半是離市的（單獨不是零）。期 初swap 價值為零，所以這些離市FRA 的價值加總為零。不要把期貨每日歸零套上來。
DER-130.core_idea: Each swap payment can be viewed as an off-market FRA; those FRA values sum to zero at initiation
DER-130.study_section: Interest-rate forwards and swaps ｜利率遠期與交換契約
DER-130.exam_trap: Treating each embedded FRA as zero because the swap price was set at par
DER-130.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-130.subtopic: 8.5 Interest-rate forwards and swaps ｜利率遠期與交換契約

DER-131.reasoning: Reasoning: Pay-fixed, receive-float: you lock in the fixed rate you pay and you collect floating. When MRR exceeds the contracted fixed rate, you collect more floating — MTM gain. Market rates up help the fixed payer. Pay-float, receive-fixed is the opposite and looks like a long fixed-rate bond.

why_wrong.B: A share put is not the mapping, and long put ̸= a duration shortcut.
why_wrong.C: The long fixed-rate-bond profile is pay-float / receive-fixed, the other side.

DER-131.zh: Pay-fixed 收浮動= 發行固定利率債去融資一張浮動利率票據（借固定、放浮動）。 利率升對這側有利。另一側才像做多固定利率債。不是股票put。
DER-131.core_idea: Pay-fixed / receive-float is a floating-rate note financed by issuing a fixed-rate bond
DER-131.study_section: Interest-rate forwards and swaps ｜利率遠期與交換契約
DER-131.exam_trap: Swapping the two vanilla sides — or replacing a swap with a put
DER-131.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-131.subtopic: 8.5 Interest-rate forwards and swaps ｜利率遠期與交換契約

DER-132.reasoning: Reasoning: Swaps are generally OTC and customizable. Many OTC derivatives may be centrally cleared or subject to margin and reporting. Compared with exchange-traded futures, OTC contracts generally retain more customization and may retain counterparty exposure when they are not centrally cleared.

why_wrong.A: The chapter is explicit: OTC ̸= unregulated.
why_wrong.B: Setting a par swap rate does not convert the contract into an exchange-traded futures.

DER-132.zh: Swap 多半是店頭、可客製。清不清算、保證金、監管要看產品與司法管轄。OTC ̸= 不受監管。定了固定利率也不會自動變成交易所期貨。
DER-132.core_idea: OTC is not a synonym for unregulated; many OTC derivatives may be centrally cleared
DER-132.study_section: Interest-rate forwards and swaps ｜利率遠期與交換契約
DER-132.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-132.subtopic: 8.5 Interest-rate forwards and swaps ｜利率遠期與交換契約

DER-133.reasoning: Reasoning: A fiduciary call (call plus a risk-free bond that pays X at T) and a protective put (share plus put) have the same payoff in every state. No-arbitrage then requires c0 + PV(X) = S0 + p0. If an equality fails, buy the cheap side and sell the expensive side.

why_wrong.A: c0 - p0 = S0 omits PV(X) and is not the parity rearrangement S0 = c0 - p0 + PV(X).
why_wrong.B: c0 + p0 = S0 is the false shortcut that also smells like long put = short stock (cancel the share).

DER-133.zh: 信託買權（call + 到期支付X 的債券）和保護性賣權（股票+ put）每個狀態 payoff 相同，所以c+PV(X)=S+p。不要寫成c+p=S（那是把put 當空股票），也不要漏掉 PV(X)。
DER-133.core_idea: Fiduciary call (call + bond that pays X at T) equals protective put (share + put)
DER-133.study_section: Put-Call Parity and a One-Period Binomial ｜買賣權平價與單期二元樹
DER-133.exam_trap: Dropping PV(X) or using long put = short stock to fake parity
DER-133.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-133.subtopic: 8.6 Put-Call Parity and a One-Period Binomial ｜買賣權平價與單期二元樹

DER-134.reasoning: Reasoning: p0 = c0 + X/(1+r)^T - S0 = 5.20 + 40/1.05 - 42 = 5.20 + 38.10 - 42 = 1.30. Rearrangements are synthetic positions, including S0 = c0 - p0 + PV(X). Use PV(X), not X, and do not replace the put with a short stock. Given: S0 = 42; X = 40; c0 = 5.20; r = 5%; T = 1; European, no dividend. Asked: p0 from parity. Formula: 5.20 + 40/1.05 −42 Variables: Bond pays X at T, so it enters as PV(X). Why this formula: Protective put = fiduciary call. The put is cheap versus the 5.20 call because the call is already ITM on a 42/40 gap. Reasonableness check: 3.20 used S - X instead of PV(X). 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。

why_wrong.B: 7.20 is 5.20 + (42 - 40), adding intrinsic instead of subtracting the financed share.
why_wrong.C: 3.20 is 5.20 - (42 - 40), using S - X instead of PV(X) — the intrinsic / lower-bound mix-up leaking into parity.

DER-134.zh: p = 5.20 + 40/1.05 - 42 = 1.30。要用執行價的現值，不要用S-X=2 去加減出3.20 或7.20。這不是long put = short 現貨。
DER-134.core_idea: Parity rearrangement: p0 = c0 + PV(X) - S0
DER-134.study_section: Put-Call Parity and a One-Period Binomial ｜買賣權平價與單期二元樹
DER-134.exam_trap: Calling S-PV(X) the call’s exercise value — leaking into parity as S-X
DER-134.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-134.subtopic: 8.6 Put-Call Parity and a One-Period Binomial ｜買賣權平價與單期二元樹

DER-135.reasoning: Reasoning: S0 = c0 - p0 + X/(1+r)^T = 4.65 - 3.10 + 80/1.040.5 = 1.55 + 78.45 = 80.00. That package is a synthetic share. It is not a long put rewritten as a short stock. Given: c0 = 4.65; p0 = 3.10; X = 80; r = 4%; T = 0.5; European, no dividend. Asked: No-arbitrage S0. Formula: 4.65 −3.10 + 80(1.04)−0.5 Variables: PV(X) is the cash that completes the fiduciary call. Why this formula: Parity solved for the share. Call minus put is not the stock until you add the financed strike. Reasonableness check: 1.55 dropped the bond. 85.75 used undiscounted X. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。

why_wrong.A: 85.75 is c0 - p0 + 80, using X instead of PV(X).
why_wrong.B: 1.55 is c0 - p0, dropping the bond that pays 80 at T.

DER-135.zh: 合成股票：S = c - p + PV(X) = 1.55 + 80/1.04^0.5 ≈80。只算c-p=1.55 是漏了 債券；直接加80 是沒用現值。
DER-135.core_idea: Synthetic share: S0 = c0 - p0 + PV(X)
DER-135.study_section: Put-Call Parity and a One-Period Binomial ｜買賣權平價與單期二元樹
DER-135.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-135.subtopic: 8.6 Put-Call Parity and a One-Period Binomial ｜買賣權平價與單期二元樹

DER-136.reasoning: Reasoning: If an equality fails, buy the cheap side and sell the expensive side. Protective put at 52.00 is rich versus fiduciary call at 51.81. Do not collapse the trade to a naked short stock. Given: S0=50; c0=6.10; p0=2.00; X=48; r=5%; T=1. Asked: Which package is cheap, and the trade. Formula: (6.10 + 48/1.05) vs (50 + 2.00) Variables: Fiduciary call vs protective put. Why this formula: Same terminal, different price. Nineteen cents is the locked gap. Reasonableness check: The reverse loses 0.19. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。
DER-136.steps: ①Fiduciary = 51.81. ②Protective = 52.00. ③Sell protective, buy fiduciary.

why_wrong.A: Buy dear / sell cheap is the wrong direction.
why_wrong.C: Parity is not long put = short stock. You need the whole fiduciary-versus-protective package.

DER-136.zh: 保護性賣權52.00 貴於信託買權51.81：賣貴的、買便宜的，鎖0.19。不要做成 「只放空股票」，那是long put = short 現貨的假捷徑。
DER-136.core_idea: If parity fails, buy the cheap side and sell the expensive side 核心觀念｜中文理解：保護性賣權52.00 貴於信託買權51.81：賣貴的、買便宜的，鎖0.19。
DER-136.study_section: Put-Call Parity and a One-Period Binomial ｜買賣權平價與單期二元樹
DER-136.exam_trap: Equating long put with short the underlying — fake parity arb
DER-136.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-136.subtopic: 8.6 Put-Call Parity and a One-Period Binomial ｜買賣權平價與單期二元樹

DER-137.reasoning: Reasoning: Put-call forward parity replaces the share with a long forward financed by a bond that pays F0(T) at settlement: F0/(1+r)^T + p0 = c0 + X/(1+r)^T, or p0 - c0 = (X - F0)/(1+r)^T = (48 - 50)/1.05 = -1.90. The long forward is the later purchase; do not rewrite it as a short stock or as a put. Given: F0 = 50; X = 48; r = 5%; T = 1. Asked: p0 - c0. Formula: (48 −50)/1.05 Variables: Same T and same X on the two options. Why this formula: A financed long forward plus a put matches a call plus a financed strike. The call is richer than the put by 1.90 because F0 exceeds X. Reasonableness check: -2.00 skipped the discount. +1.90 flipped the gap. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。

why_wrong.B: -2.00 is (48 - 50) without discounting.
why_wrong.C: 1.90 flips X - F0.

DER-137.zh: 遠期平價：p-c = (X-F)/(1+r)^T = (48-50)/1.05 = -1.90。不要忘了折現（-2.00）， 也不要把正負弄反。遠期是以後買，不是put，也不是空股票。
DER-137.core_idea: Put-call forward parity: p0 - c0 = (X - F0(T))/(1+r)^T
DER-137.study_section: Put-Call Parity and a One-Period Binomial ｜買賣權平價與單期二元樹
DER-137.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-137.subtopic: 8.6 Put-Call Parity and a One-Period Binomial ｜買賣權平價與單期二元樹

DER-138.reasoning: Reasoning: The underlying today is S0. Next period it is one of two prices, Su or Sd. A call then pays cu = max(0, Su - X) or cd = max(0, Sd - X). Here cu = max(0, 100 - 80) = 20, cd = max(0, 64 - 80) = 0. Payoffs are computed before ∆, before the bond, and before any probability. Given: S0=80; Su=100; Sd=64; X=80; European call. Asked: cu and cd (step 2 of the seven-step walk). Formula: max(0, 100 −80), max(0, 64 −80) Variables: Payoff first; pricing later. Why this formula: Expiration value of the right in each live state. The call is OTM if the down move occurs. Reasonableness check: 16 and the raw prices are not call payoffs. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。

why_wrong.B: A call pays max(0, S - X), not S - S0. Down: max(0, 64 - 80) = 0, not 16.
why_wrong.C: The underlying’s levels are inputs, not the call’s payoffs.

DER-138.zh: 先算兩個狀態的payoff：上漲max(0,100-80)=20，下跌max(0,64-80)=0。不要把 股價或股價變動幅度當成選擇權損益。
DER-138.core_idea: Walk the tree in order: S0, Su, Sd, then the option payoffs in each state
DER-138.study_section: Put-Call Parity and a One-Period Binomial ｜買賣權平價與單期二元樹
DER-138.formula:
cu = max(0, Su −X),
cd = max(0, Sd −X)
DER-138.source_note: 解答依據 DER_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Derivatives。
DER-138.subtopic: 8.6 Put-Call Parity and a One-Period Binomial ｜買賣權平價與單期二元樹

DER-139.reasoning: Reasoning: ∆= (cu - cd)/(Su - Sd) = (20 - 0)/(100 - 64) = 20/36 = 0.5556 ≈0.56. Choose ∆ so the two states cancel. This is shares per option for a call, not the statement that a call equals a share, and not a put rewritten as a short stock. Given: cu=20; cd=0; Su=100; Sd=64. Asked: ∆, shares per call. Formula: (20 −0)/(100 −64) Variables: Positive for this call because cu > cd. Why this formula: Same ∆in both states cancels the underlying move against the option move. About 5/9 of a share hedges one call. Reasonableness check: 1.00 is the false stock identity. -0.56 is a put-style sign. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。

why_wrong.B: Negative ∆is the usual put sign, not this call’s (cu - cd) > 0.
why_wrong.C: 1.00 would be “one share per call,” a stock-equivalence shortcut. ∆is 20/36 = 0.555…≈ 0.56.

DER-139.zh: ∆= (20-0)/(100-64) = 20/36 ≈0.56。這是讓漲跌兩態互相抵銷的避險比率，不 是「一張call 等於一股」，更不是put = 空股票。
DER-139.core_idea: Hedge ratio ∆= (cu - cd)/(Su - Sd) makes the two states cancel

DER-140.reasoning: Reasoning: Down-state match: 0.5556 × 64 = 1.04 B ⇒B = 34.19. The replicating portfolio holds ∆shares and borrows B so both states match the option. That portfolio is riskless, so it grows at r. No-arbitrage: the option’s value today equals the replicating portfolio’s value today: c0 = 0.5556 × 80 - 34.19 = 10.26. Steps so far: S0/Su/Sd; payoffs; ∆; replicating (∆, B). Given: ∆= 0.5556; Sd = 64; S0 = 80; r = 4%; cu = 20; cd = 0. Asked: B and c0 from the replicating portfolio. Formula: B = 0.5556 × 64/1.04; c0 = 0.5556 × 80 −34.19 Variables: B is the amount borrowed today; it grows at r. Why this formula: Down state: share piece equals the loan repayment because cd = 0. Borrowing 34.19 against 0.56 share replicates the 20-or-0 call. Reasonableness check: Using 35.56 as B skips the discount. Dropping B is ∆S0. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。

why_wrong.B: 35.56 is ∆× 64, the down-state share value, not the amount borrowed today. Divide by 1.04.
why_wrong.C: Dropping B treats the call as ∆shares, the stock-equivalence shortcut.

DER-140.zh: 下跌態：0.5556×64 = 1.04B ⇒B=34.19。複製組合是∆股減掉借入的B，今天 價值44.44-34.19=10.26。不要把35.56 當今天的借款，更不要丟掉融資腿把call 當成0.56 股。
DER-140.core_idea: Replicating portfolio: hold ∆shares and borrow B so both states match the option 核心觀念｜中文理解：下跌態：0.5556×64 = 1.04B ⇒B=34.19。

DER-141.reasoning: Reasoning: Step 1: S0 = 40, Su = 48, Sd = 32. Step 2: cu = max(0, 48 - 36) = 12, cd = max(0, 32 - 36) = 0. Step 3: ∆= (12 - 0)/(48 - 32) = 0.75. Step 4: Replicating portfolio holds 0.75 share and borrows B; down-state match 0.75 × 32 = 1.05 B ⇒B = 22.86. Step 5: Both states then match the call, so the package is riskless. Step 6: A riskless package is discounted (or financed) at r. Step 7: c0 = 0.75 × 40 - 22.86 = 7.14. Risk-neutral check: u = 1.20, d = 0.80, π* = (1.05 - 0.80)/(1.20 - 0.80) = 0.625, c0 = (0.625 × 12 + 0.375 × 0)/1.05 = 7.14. π* is a pricing probability, not a forecast that the real world rises with probability 0.625. Given: S0=40; Su=48; Sd=32; X=36; one-period r=5%; European call. Asked: No-arbitrage c0 after the full seven-step walk. Formula: 0.75 × 40 −0.75 × 32/1.05 Variables: u=Su/S0=1.20; d=0.80. π* is not a real-world forecast. Why this formula: Replicating portfolio equals the call in both states, hence today. Three-quarters of a share, financed with 22.86 of borrowing, is the call. Reasonableness check: 6.00 averages undiscounted payoffs. 12.00 is cu. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。
DER-141.steps: ①Nodes: 40, 48, 32. ②Payoffs: 12 and 0. ③∆= 12/16 = 0.75. ④B = 24 / 1.05 = 22.86. ⑤Riskless match in both states. ⑥Finance / discount at 5%. ⑦c0 = 30 - 22.86 = 7.14.

why_wrong.B: 6.00 is the average of 12 and 0, a real-world 50/50 with no discount — or a raw (Su-X)/2 style shortcut.
why_wrong.C: 12.00 is the up-state payoff, undiscounted and unweighted.

DER-141.zh: 七步：節點40/48/32 →payoff 12 與0 →∆=0.75 →複製（0.75 股、借22.86） →兩態相同所以無風險→用5% 折現／融資→今天7.14。不要平均兩個payoff，也不要直 接報上漲態12。π* 是定價用機率，不是預測。
DER-141.core_idea: Full seven-step one-period binomial: S0/Su/Sd, payoffs, ∆, replicating, riskless, discount, value 核心觀念｜中文理解：七步：節點40/48/32 →payoff 12 與0 →∆=0.75 →複製（0.75 股、借22.86）→ 兩態相同所以無風險→用5% 折現／融資→今天7.14。

DER-142.reasoning: Reasoning: The equivalent risk-neutral method uses a pricing probability, not a forecast of the real-world up-move. π* = [(1+r) - d]/(u - d), and c0 = [π* cu + (1-π*) cd]/(1+r). Discount at r because π* was built so the underlying’s expected return equals r.

why_wrong.B: Two states do not imply 50/50. π* is built from u, d, and r.
why_wrong.C: π* is not a weather forecast of the stock, and the chapter discounts the risk-neutral expectation at r, not at a risk-adjusted equity rate.

DER-142.zh: π* 是定價用機率，讓標的在這套機率下的期望報酬等於r，所以可以用r 折現。 它不是在預測真實世界上漲機率，也不是看到兩個狀態就各1/2。
DER-142.core_idea: π* = [(1+r) - d]/(u - d) is a pricing probability, not a real-world forecast 核心觀念｜中文理解：π* 是定價用機率，讓標的在這套機率下的期望報酬等於r，所以可以用r 折現。

DER-143.reasoning: Reasoning: π* = (1.04 - 0.80)/(1.25 - 0.80) = 0.24/0.45 = 0.5333. c0 = (0.5333 × 20 + 0.4667 × 0)/1.04 = 10.26. Same value as the replicating portfolio. π* is not a statement that the real world has a 53% chance of the up move. Given: u=1.25; d=0.80; r=4%; cu=20; cd=0. Asked: π* and c0. Formula: (1.04 −0.80)/(1.25 −0.80); (0.533 × 20)/1.04 Variables: π* is built from u, d, r only — no real-world p. Why this formula: π* makes E*[S1] = S0(1+r), so discounting at r is valid. Pricing probability 53.3%, not a forecast. Reasonableness check: 0.50 and 0.625 belong to other assumptions. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。

why_wrong.A: 0.625 is (1.05 - 0.80)/(1.20 - 0.80) from a different tree (u = 1.20, d = 0.80, r = 5%). Do not import another example’s π*.
why_wrong.B: 0.50 is not implied by u, d, r. Even 0.5 × 20 = 10 still needs to be divided by 1.04.

DER-143.core_idea: Compute π* and the discounted risk-neutral expectation — still not a real-world probability 核心觀念｜中文理解：π* = (1.04-0.80)/(1.25-0.80)=0.533，折現後call=10.26。

DER-144.reasoning: Reasoning: If the call is underpriced relative to the model, buy the call, short ∆of the underlying, and lend; the package earns more than r. If overpriced, reverse the hedge. Different price (6.40 vs the book’s “underpriced relative to 5.95”) and different ∆.

why_wrong.A: Long call plus long stock does not cancel the two states and is not financed to beat r risklessly.
why_wrong.C: Write-call / buy-stock is the overpriced-call hedge.

DER-144.zh: Call 被低估：買call、按∆放空標的、去放貸，組合賺超過r。高估才是賣call、 買標的。不要又買call 又買股票——那沒對沖，也不是無風險超額。

DER-145.reasoning: Reasoning: Step 1: S0 = 60, Su = 75, Sd = 48. Step 2: pu = max(0, 66 - 75) = 0, pd = max(0, 66 - 48) = 18. Step 3: ∆= (0 - 18)/(75 - 48) = -18/27 = -0.6667 (short 2/3 share per long put — not “short one share,” and not long put = short stock). Step 4: Replicating: short 0.6667 share and lend B so the up state matches 0: -0.6667 × 75 + 1.06 B = 0 ⇒B = 47.17. Step 5: Down state: -0.6667 × 48 + 1.06 × 47.17 = 18, so both states match — riskless. Step 6: Discount / finance at 6%. Step 7: p0 = ∆S0 + B = -0.6667 × 60 + 47.17 = 7.17. Check: u = 1.25, d = 0.80, π* = (1.06 - 0.80)/(1.25 - 0.80) = 0.5778, p0 = (0.5778 × 0 + 0.4222 × 18)/1.06 = 7.17. π* prices; it does not forecast the real-world down move. Given: S0=60; Su=75; Sd=48; X=66; r=6%; European put. Asked: No-arbitrage p0 after the full seven-step walk. Formula: ∆= −18/27; π∗= (1.06 −0.80)/(1.25 −0.80); p0 = (0.4222 × 18)/1.06 Variables: ∆is negative for this put but not -1. π* is a pricing probability. Why this formula: Same replication logic as the call, with put payoffs. A long put is a short fraction of the share plus a long bond — not a naked short stock. Reasonableness check: 9.00 is a 50/50 average. 18.00 is pd. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。
DER-145.steps: ①Nodes 60 / 75 / 48. ②Payoffs 0 and 18. ③∆= -0.6667. ④Lend B = 47.17. ⑤Both states match ⇒riskless. ⑥Use r = 6%. ⑦p0 = -40 + 47.17 = 7.17.

why_wrong.A: 18.00 is the down-state payoff, undiscounted.
why_wrong.C: 9.00 averages 0 and 18, a 50/50 undiscounted shortcut (and a real-world-probability smell).

DER-145.zh: 七步走完：payoff 0 與18，∆=-2/3（不是空一股），放貸47.17，兩態對齊所以無 風險，用6% 計價，put=7.17。不要平均0 和18，也不要直接報18。Long put ̸= short 現貨； π* 不是真實世界機率。
DER-145.core_idea: A one-period put uses max(0, X - S) in each state; ∆is then negative; π* is still not a real-world probability 核心觀念｜中文理解：七步走完：payoff 0 與18，∆=-2/3（不是空一股），放貸47.17，兩態對齊所以無風 險，用6% 計價，put=7.17。

AI-001.reasoning: Reasoning: Alternative investments are defined by what the curriculum includes under that heading: hedge funds, private equity, real estate, commodities, infrastructure, and a smaller set such as patents and collectibles. They differ from traditional public stocks and bonds in the assets held and in the vehicles used to hold them.

why_wrong.A: Public investment-grade bonds are traditional fixed income, not the alts heading.
why_wrong.C: Listed large-cap equity in an index fund is traditional public equity.

AI-001.zh: 另類投資先看課程把什麼放進這一欄：對沖基金、PE、不動產、商品、基礎建設， 再加上專利、收藏品這類較小項目。公債與大盤股票不是另類，只因為「比較特別」不能自己 加進去。

AI-002.reasoning: Reasoning: Relative to traditional assets, alternatives typically have less liquidity, more manager specialization, less regulation and transparency, thinner and more problematic return histories, and different legal and tax treatment. Managers may use derivatives and leverage, short securities, and buy claims that do not trade.

why_wrong.B: The sources list less liquidity, thinner and more problematic histories, and different legal/tax treatment — the reverse of this choice.
why_wrong.C: Legal and tax treatment differs; the vehicle is part of what makes the holding “alternative.”

AI-002.zh: 另類通常比較不流動、更靠經理人、較不透明、歷史報酬也較薄。不要把它想成 「跟股票債券一樣，只是名字不同」。
AI-002.core_idea: Alternatives typically have less liquidity, more specialization, less transparency, and thinner return histories

AI-003.reasoning: Reasoning: The usual portfolio case is a historically low correlation with traditional assets, which can reduce overall portfolio risk, plus historically higher average returns. Those extra returns are attributed to less efficient pricing, compensation for illiquidity, and the use of leverage. The same data are not clean.

why_wrong.B: The same data are not clean: public-asset risk statistics often miss the risk that matters here.
why_wrong.C: The sources do not guarantee a higher Sharpe ratio for every series.

AI-003.zh: 放進組合的理由，主要是跟股債較不同步，加上歷史平均報酬較高；不是保證夏 普一定比較高，也不是風險數字可以直接套用公開資產那一套。
AI-003.core_idea: The portfolio case is historically low correlation plus historically higher average returns

AI-004.reasoning: Reasoning: Extra returns are attributed to less efficient pricing, illiquidity compensation, and leverage. That is not a claim that the printed averages are unbiased. Survivorship bias and backfill bias pull sample means up because failures and weak early years are missing. Public-asset risk statistics often miss the risk that matters for illiquid, leveraged vehicles.

why_wrong.A: Survivorship and backfill pull reported averages up, not down.
why_wrong.B: The sources do not require daily public-style marks; illiquid holdings may be marked to model.

AI-004.zh: 較高平均報酬來自定價較不效率、流動性補償、槓桿；但你看到的歷史數字常被 存活者與回填往上拉。不要把「歷史比較高」當成乾淨的超額。
AI-004.core_idea: Extra reported returns are attributed to inefficient pricing, illiquidity, and leverage — and the histories are biased

AI-005.reasoning: Reasoning: Survivorship bias: if the sample keeps only funds that still exist, average returns are too high, because the failures are missing. That is a separate problem from backfill (inserting a prior track record when a fund is added) and from selection bias (voluntary reporting).

why_wrong.A: The last NAV of a dead fund is not kept if the sample retains only funds that still exist.
why_wrong.C: Survivorship removes failures; it does not leave a conservative (too-low) mean.

AI-005.zh: 樣本只留還活著的基金，失敗的報酬被拿掉，平均就被拉高。這叫存活者偏誤， 不是「最後一筆NAV 已經代表死亡」。
AI-005.core_idea: Survivorship bias keeps only funds that still exist, so average returns are too high

AI-006.reasoning: Reasoning: Backfill bias: when a fund is added to an index, its prior track record is inserted; funds get added after they have already done well, so past averages are again pulled up. That is distinct from survivorship (dropping dead funds) and from selection bias (voluntary reporting).

why_wrong.A: The definition of backfill is that the prior track record is inserted, so past averages change.
why_wrong.C: Backfill is not a J-curve adjustment, and it does not pull means down.

AI-006.zh: 基金是表現好了才被加進資料庫，還把加入前的成績一併寫進去，過去平均就被 拉高。這是回填，不是J 曲線，也不是「只算加入之後」。
AI-006.core_idea: Backfill bias inserts a fund’s prior track record after it has already done well

AI-007.reasoning: Reasoning: Hedge-fund databases suffer from selection bias because reporting is voluntary. Combined with survivorship and backfill, the printed average is a poor stand-in for the return an LP should expect.

why_wrong.A: Waterfall type is a distribution rule, not the reason the database is biased.
why_wrong.B: Mutual-fund reporting mandates are not the hedge-fund database problem described here.

AI-007.zh: 對沖基金資料庫是自願申報，願意報的本來就不是隨機樣本。這跟「共同基金依 法申報」或「只有歐洲瀑布才能報」無關。
AI-007.core_idea: Selection bias arises because hedge-fund database reporting is voluntary

AI-008.reasoning: Reasoning: Three access routes, in increasing investor control: fund investment (choose a manager; capital is pre-committed before investments are selected), co-investment (invest alongside the fund in a specific deal), and direct investment (the investor selects and holds the asset; no fund-level decisions are delegated). Co-investment is used to accelerate deployment when remaining fund capital or expected inflows cannot cover the deal, to widen available investments, or to diversify an existing fund pool.

why_wrong.B: The original fund commitment is fund investment; this extra ticket is a deallevel co-invest, not another blind-pool subscription.
why_wrong.C: Co-investing does not make the LP the GP, and it does not transfer fund-level decision rights.

AI-008.zh: 共同投資是跟基金一起做「這一筆」交易，常用在基金剩額不夠或想加快部署。這 不是再簽一檔盲池，也不是LP 變成GP。
AI-008.core_idea: Co-investment puts capital alongside the fund in a specific deal; direct investment selects the asset
AI-008.study_section: Structures and Economics ｜結構與經濟機制

AI-009.reasoning: Reasoning: Hedge funds and private equity funds are typically limited partnerships. Investors are limited partners (LPs). The manager is the general partner (GP). The common hedge-fund fee quote is “2 and 20”: a management fee of 2% of AUM plus an incentive fee (carried interest) of 20% of profits.

why_wrong.A: LPs are the outside investors; they do not charge the 2-and-20.
why_wrong.B: Managers are typically required to invest their own capital; the GP is not recast as a custodian.

AI-009.zh: 經理人是GP，出資的投資人是LP。2 和20 是GP 收的，不是LP 收的。
AI-009.core_idea: Hedge funds and PE funds are typically LPs; investors are LPs and the manager is the GP
AI-009.study_section: Structures and Economics ｜結構與經濟機制
AI-009.source_note: 解答依據 AI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Alternative Investments。

AI-010.reasoning: Reasoning: Private equity management fees are typically 1% to 3% of committed capital — the amount the LP has agreed to provide — not of capital already invested. Committed capital is drawn down, usually over three to five years, as deals are found. Hedge-fund style management fees are a percentage of AUM, on invested capital. Charging PE fees on committed capital is why early years can show negative returns before much capital is even at work.

why_wrong.A: PE management fees start with the commitment; they are not waived until exit. American waterfalls affect incentive timing, not this management-fee base.
why_wrong.C: Residual-value fees are not the typical PE management-fee base in the sources.

AI-010.zh: PE 管理費通常按承諾資本1%–3% 收，不是按已call 出去的錢。承諾額還沒投 入，費用已經在抽，所以早期報酬可以是負的。對沖基金才比較像按AUM ／已投資本。
AI-010.core_idea: PE management fees are typically 1% to 3% of committed capital, not of capital already invested

AI-011.reasoning: Reasoning: The notes’ independent-of-management-fee calculation is R_GP = P1 rm + max[0,(P1-P0)p]. Substitute P1=250, P0=200, rm=0.02, p=0.20: management fee = 250×0.02 = 5; incentive = 50×0.20 = 10; R_GP = 15. LP return r_i = (P1-P0-R_GP)/P0 = (50-15)/200 = 17.5%. Independent versus net changes the LP result; both conventions are used. Given: P0=200; P1=250 before fees; rm=2% of ending value; p=20% of the gain, independent of the management fee; no hurdle; no HWM shortfall. Asked: LP periodic return after fees. Formula: RGP = P1rm + max[0, (P1 −P0)p] Variables: P0, P1 beginning and ending fund values; rm management-fee rate on ending AUM; p incentive-fee rate; R_GP total GP fees; r_i LP periodic return. Why this formula: Independent incentive uses the whole value gain as the carried-interest base; management fee is a separate layer on ending AUM. The LP earns what remains after both layers. A 25% gross gain becomes 17.5% to the LP after 2-and-20 taken independently. Reasonableness check: 22.5% drops the incentive layer. 25% is the gross gain. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。

why_wrong.B: Uses the pretax gain, 50/200 = 25.0%, and ignores both fee layers.
why_wrong.C: Subtracts only the management fee: (50 - 5)/200 = 22.5%.

AI-011.zh: 獨立計激勵費時，增值50 全部當基數：管理費5、激勵費10，共15。LP 報酬是 (50-15)/200=17.5%。不要只扣管理費，也不要把25% 毛漲幅當成LP 拿到的。
AI-011.core_idea: Independent incentive: R_GP = P1 rm + max[0,(P1-P0)p]; LP return uses that total fee

AI-012.reasoning: Reasoning: Net of the management fee, the gain base is P1(1-rm)-P0 = 250×0.98 - 200 = 45. Incentive = 45×0.20 = 9. Management fee = 5. R_GP = 14. r_i = (50-14)/200 = 18.0%. The same 200-to-250 path produced 17.5% when incentive was independent. Independent versus net changes the LP result; both conventions are used. Given: P0=200; P1=250 before fees; rm=2% of ending value; incentive 20% of the gain net of the management fee; no hurdle. Asked: LP periodic return after fees. Formula: RGP = P1rm + max{0, [P1(1 −rm) −P0]p} Variables: The gain base is ending value after the management fee, minus beginning value. Why this formula: Net-of-fee incentive shrinks the carried-interest base by the management fee taken on ending AUM. Netting the management fee before carry raises the LP return relative to the independent 17.5% on the same path. Reasonableness check: 17.5% is the independent convention. 22.5% ignores carry. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。
AI-012.steps: ①Management fee = 250 × 0.02 = 5. Value after that fee = 245. ②Gain base = 245 - 200 = 45. Incentive = 45 × 0.20 = 9. ③R_GP = 5 + 9 = 14. ④r_i = (250 - 200 - 14) / 200 = 36 / 200 = 18.0%.

why_wrong.A: Subtracts only the management fee and skips incentive: (50-5)/200=22.5%.
why_wrong.B: Uses the independent convention: incentive on the full 50, R_GP=15, r_i=17.5%.

AI-012.zh: 激勵費若先扣管理費，基數是245-200=45，激勵費9，總費用14，LP 得到18%。 同一條路徑若獨立計激勵費是17.5%。題幹寫net of the management fee，不要用獨立公式。
AI-012.core_idea: Incentive net of management fee uses [P1(1-rm)-P0] as the gain base

AI-013.reasoning: Reasoning: The notes’ third workable formula is R_GP = P1 rm + max0, [P1(1-rm)-P0(1+h)] p. Substitute P1=250, P0=200, rm=0.02, h=0.08, p=0.20: management fee = 5; net-of-fee terminal = 245; hurdle amount on beginning value = 200×1.08 = 216; incentive base = 245-216 = 29; incentive = 5.8; R_GP = 10.8; r_i = (50-10.8)/200 = 19.6%. The hurdle is the minimum fund return the GP must clear before earning an incentive fee; this formula charges carry only on the return above that hurdle, after the management fee. Given: P0=200; P1=250 before fees; rm=2% of ending value; p=20%; hurdle h=8%; incentive net of the management fee and above the hurdle. Asked: LP periodic return after fees. Formula: RGP = P1rm + max{0, [P1(1 −rm) −P0(1 + h)]p} Variables: h is the hurdle (preferred return). The incentive base subtracts P0(1+h) after removing the management fee from P1. Why this formula: The structure charges carry only on value above the preferred-return path, after the management fee, which is one of the two hurdle bases in the notes (fee only on the return above the hurdle). The 8% hurdle shrinks carry relative to the no-hurdle net case (R_GP 14 → 10.8), so the LP keeps more. Reasonableness check: 18.0% is net of management fee with no hurdle. 17.5% is independent 2-and-20. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。

why_wrong.A: Uses independent 2-and-20 with no hurdle: r_i=17.5%.
why_wrong.C: Drops the hurdle and uses net-of-management-fee incentive only: r_i=18.0%.

AI-013.zh: 有門檻且激勵費在管理費之後算：245 減去200×1.08=216，基數只剩29，激勵費 5.8，總費用10.8，LP 報酬19.6%。不要改用沒有門檻的net 或獨立公式。
AI-013.core_idea: Net-of-fees hurdle: incentive base is P1(1-rm)-P0(1+h)

AI-014.reasoning: Reasoning: Profit may be defined as any gain in value, the gain net of the management fee, or the gain above a hurdle. Two calculation bases are used: fee only on the return above the hurdle; or fee on the entire profit, but only if the hurdle is met. The notes’ third formula implements the first of those bases, net of the management fee.

why_wrong.A: Catch-up can give the GP 100% of incremental distributions until the stated share is reached; it is not “100% until LPs double,” and hedge funds do use incentive fees.
why_wrong.B: HWM and exit timing are different mechanics; they do not replace the two hurdle bases.

AI-014.zh: 門檻有兩種算法：只對超過門檻的那一段抽；或門檻過了就對整段利潤抽。不要 跟高水位、逐筆退出混成同一件事。
AI-014.core_idea: Two hurdle bases: fee only on the return above the hurdle, or fee on the entire profit if the hurdle is met
AI-014.study_section: Structures and Economics ｜結構與經濟機制

AI-015.reasoning: Reasoning: R_GP = P1 rm + max0, [P1(1-rm)-P0(1+h)] p. Management fee = 420×0.02 = 8.4. P1(1-rm) = 411.6. P0(1+h) = 400×1.10 = 440. Incentive base = 411.6-440 = -28.4 →max with 0 is 0. R_GP = 8.4. A hurdle is the minimum the GP must clear before earning an incentive fee; here that test fails. Given: P0=400; P1=420 before fees; rm=2% of ending value; p=20%; h=10%; incentive net of the management fee and above the hurdle. Asked: Total GP fees R_GP. Formula: RGP = P1rm + max{0, [P1(1 −rm) −P0(1 + h)]p} Variables: The max[0, ·] clause zeros the incentive when the net-of-fee value does not clear P0(1+h). Why this formula: Carry is not earned until the hurdle path is cleared. The management fee on ending AUM is still charged. A 5% gross gain does not clear a 10% hurdle after fees, so only the management fee is paid. Reasonableness check: Any positive carry on this path ignores the max[0, ·] hurdle test. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。

why_wrong.A: Uses net-of-management-fee carry and drops the hurdle: base 411.6-400=11.6, carry 2.32, total 10.72.
why_wrong.B: Applies independent carry to the raw 20 gain: 8.4 + 4.0 = 12.4 is not even listed; 16.4 invents a larger carry on that 20.

AI-015.zh: 先算管理費8.4。門檻後的基數411.6-440 是負的，激勵費為0。GP 只拿到管理 費。不要在門檻沒過時仍對毛增值或扣完管理費的增值抽20%。
AI-015.core_idea: If the net-of-fees hurdle base is negative, incentive is zero and only the management fee is paid

AI-016.reasoning: Reasoning: A high-water mark is the highest fund value net of fees previously reached. Incentive fees are paid only on gains above that mark, so LPs are not charged twice for the same recovery. The path from 100 to 115 is a recovery toward 120, not a new high.

why_wrong.A: A positive year does not waive the mark; the point of the HWM is that LPs are not charged twice for the same recovery.
why_wrong.C: HWM is stated for incentive fees generally, including hedge-fund style fees; it is not confined to PE European waterfalls.

AI-016.zh: 高水位是以前扣完費後到過的最高點。從100 漲回115 還在120 下面，這段是 「賺回來」，不能再抽一次激勵費。不要以為今年正報酬就重設，也不要把HWM 說成只有PE 歐洲瀑布才有。
AI-016.core_idea: A high-water mark is the highest prior net-of-fee value; carry is not charged twice for the same recovery
AI-016.study_section: Structures and Economics ｜結構與經濟機制
AI-016.exam_trap: Charging incentive again on a recovery below the high-water mark
AI-016.source_note: 解答依據 AI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Alternative Investments。

AI-017.reasoning: Reasoning: Independent fees: R_GP = 180×0.02 + (180-150)×0.20 = 3.6 + 6.0 = 9.6. Ending capital in the fund is P1-R_GP = 180-9.6 = 170.4. A high-water mark is the highest fund value net of fees previously reached. After fees in year 1, the mark used in year 2 is that net value. Given: Year-1 P0=150; P1=180 before fees; rm=2% of ending value; p=20% independent; no hurdle. Asked: High-water mark used in year 2. Formula: HWM2 = P1 −RGP Variables: Ending capital in the fund equals P1 minus total GP fees. That net value is the mark after a profitable year. Why this formula: Incentive is paid only on gains above the highest prior net-of-fee value. After year-1 fees, that value is P1-R_GP. Carry and the management fee both come out before the new peak is locked in. Reasonableness check: 180 is pretax. 150 is the old start, not the new net peak. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。

why_wrong.B: Leaves the mark at the year-1 start, as if a profitable year did not raise the net peak.
why_wrong.C: Uses the pretax ending value and never subtracts year-1 fees.

AI-017.zh: 第一年獨立2 和20：費用3.6+6=9.6，淨值170.4。高水位用的是扣完費後的最高 點，不是毛值180，也不是年初150。
AI-017.core_idea: After fees in year 1, the high-water mark used in year 2 is that net value
AI-017.study_section: Structures and Economics ｜結構與經濟機制
AI-017.source_note: 解答依據 AI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Alternative Investments。

AI-018.reasoning: Reasoning: Management fee = 260×0.02 = 5.2. Incentive is paid only on gains above the mark: (260-240)×0.20 = 4.0. R_GP = 9.2. r_i = (260-210-9.2)/210 = 40.8/210 = 19.43%. Using P1-P0 as the carry base would charge LPs again on the recovery from 210 to 240 — the double-charge the high-water mark is designed to stop. Given: HWM=240; P0=210; P1=260 before fees; rm=2% of ending value; p=20% of the gain above the HWM, independent of the management fee; no hurdle. Asked: LP periodic return after fees. Formula: RGP = P1rm + max[0, (P1 −HWM)p] Variables: Incentive base is P1 minus the high-water mark, not P1 minus this year’s P0, when P0 is below the mark. Why this formula: The high-water mark replaces the ordinary P1-P0 gain whenever that gain includes a recovery already paid for in an earlier period. Only the 20 of new high-water value is carried; the 30 of recovery is not. Reasonableness check: 16.6% carries the recovery. 23.8% is the gross year gain. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。

why_wrong.A: Uses the pretax year gain, 50/210=23.8%, and ignores both fees.
why_wrong.B: Charges 20% on the full 50 year gain (210 to 260), so R_GP=5.2+10=15.2 and r_i=34.8/210=16.6%.

AI-018.zh: 管理費按期末260 收5.2。激勵費只對超過高水位240 的20 抽，等於4，總費用 9.2。LP 報酬(50-9.2)/210≈19.4%。若對整段50 抽，等於把210 漲回240 再剝一次。
AI-018.core_idea: Year-2 incentive uses gains above the high-water mark, not the full year gain from a lower start
AI-018.study_section: Structures and Economics ｜結構與經濟機制
AI-018.exam_trap: Charging incentive again on a recovery below the high-water mark

AI-019.reasoning: Reasoning: A catch-up clause favors the GP. Once the hurdle is cleared, the GP may receive 100% of additional distributions until the GP has received its stated share of total profit (20% in the usual example); only then is the remainder split 80/20 between LPs and GP. Clawback is the opposite-direction protection for LPs.

why_wrong.B: Reclaiming excessive GP fees when later deals disappoint is a clawback, not catch-up.
why_wrong.C: Catch-up operates after the hurdle is cleared; it does not delete the hurdle.

AI-019.zh: 追補是門檻過了以後，先讓GP 拿到約定的那20% 利潤份額（這段可100% 給 GP），之後才80/20。不要把追補看成「取消門檻」，也不要看成clawback。
AI-019.core_idea: A catch-up clause favors the GP: 100% of additional distributions until the stated profit share is reached
AI-019.study_section: Structures and Economics ｜結構與經濟機制
AI-019.source_note: 解答依據 AI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Alternative Investments。
AI-019.subtopic: 9.1 Structures and Economics ｜結構與經濟機制

AI-020.reasoning: Reasoning: A clawback lets LPs reclaim GP incentive fees so that, over the life of the fund, LPs receive their capital back and the agreed share of total profit. The situation arises when early deals are strong and later deals are not. One formulation: the GP must return fees that would otherwise leave LPs with less than 80% of the profits.

why_wrong.A: Clawback adjusts incentive, not the contracted management-fee base.
why_wrong.C: Clawback exists precisely because early GP fees can prove excessive when later deals disappoint; it is not a rule that locks American fees in place, and the sources do not confine it to one waterfall.

AI-020.zh: Clawback 是後期變差時，把GP 前期多拿的激勵費要回來，讓整檔生命期仍接近 約定的利潤拆分（常見表述是LP 至少留80% 利潤）。不是用來加管理費，也不是禁止調整。
AI-020.core_idea: Clawback lets LPs reclaim GP incentive so that, over the life of the fund, LPs keep the agreed profit share
AI-020.study_section: Structures and Economics ｜結構與經濟機制
AI-020.source_note: 解答依據 AI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Alternative Investments。
AI-020.subtopic: 9.1 Structures and Economics ｜結構與經濟機制

AI-021.reasoning: Reasoning: Waterfalls decide when the GP is paid. Deal-by-deal (American): incentive can be collected on each exited deal, even before LPs have received their capital back or preferred return — advantageous to the GP. Whole-of-fund (European): the GP takes no profit until LPs have their capital back and the hurdle is met. Private equity incentive fees are typically not earned until investors’ initial capital has been returned — the European pattern.

why_wrong.A: PE incentive is carried interest on profit, not a relabeling of the committedcapital management fee.
why_wrong.C: Whole-of-fund (European) is the settlement that waits; American is the opposite.

AI-021.zh: 美國瀑布是「這一筆賺了就可以先抽」；歐洲是整檔先還本金與門檻。還有公司沒 賣、本金沒還完，美國瀑布仍可能讓GP 先拿carry。
AI-021.core_idea: Deal-by-deal (American) waterfalls let the GP take carry per exit before LPs are made whole
AI-021.study_section: Structures and Economics ｜結構與經濟機制
AI-021.exam_trap: Reading deal-by-deal waterfalls as LP-friendly whole-of-fund settlement
AI-021.source_note: 解答依據 AI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Alternative Investments。
AI-021.subtopic: 9.1 Structures and Economics ｜結構與經濟機制

AI-022.reasoning: Reasoning: A lockup is the minimum holding period before withdrawal; a notice period is the delay between a redemption request and payment; a gate lets the manager limit redemptions for a time; a redemption fee discourages exit and offsets trading costs imposed on remaining investors.

why_wrong.A: Catch-up and waterfalls govern distribution of profit, not the redemption queue.
why_wrong.B: HWM and clawback govern incentive calculation and recapture, not redemption timing.

AI-022.zh: 閉鎖期過了還要等通知期才拿得到錢；閘門是限制這一期能贖回多少。不要把這 些流通性摩擦跟HWM、clawback、瀑布搞在一起。
AI-022.core_idea: Lockup is the minimum hold; notice is the delay after a request; a gate limits redemptions
AI-022.study_section: Structures and Economics ｜結構與經濟機制
AI-022.source_note: 解答依據 AI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Alternative Investments。

AI-023.reasoning: Reasoning: Custom terms include fees tied to liquidity or account size, founder shares with a lower management fee for early investors, and either/or fees (a large investor chooses a lower management fee or a higher incentive fee).

why_wrong.A: Founder shares and either/or elections are fee terms; they are not automatic lifetime redemption blocks.
why_wrong.B: Waterfall and clawback are distribution-of-profit rules, not a lower management-fee share class.

AI-023.zh: 創始份額是早期投資人管理費較低；either/or 是大戶在「較低管理費」與「較高 激勵費」裡選一個。這不是瀑布，也不是鎖死贖回。
AI-023.core_idea: Custom terms include founder shares with a lower management fee and either/or fee elections
AI-023.study_section: Structures and Economics ｜結構與經濟機制

AI-024.reasoning: Reasoning: A fund of funds charges its own layer, commonly “1 and 10,” on top of the underlying funds’ fees. Funds of funds are the multi-manager wrapper: diversification across strategies and access for smaller investors, at a second fee layer.

why_wrong.A: The FoF layer is itself a management-plus-incentive quote; it is not illegal.
why_wrong.C: The sources do not waive underlying 2-and-20 because a wrapper is used.

AI-024.zh: FoF 自己再收一層，常見1 和10，底下基金的2 和20 通常還在。換來的是分散 與較小額度的入場，不是比較便宜。
AI-024.core_idea: A fund of funds charges its own layer, commonly 1 and 10, on top of the underlying funds’ fees

AI-025.reasoning: Reasoning: The private-capital cycle is capital commitment (selection, capital calls, often negative reported returns) →capital deployment →capital distribution. Plotted against time, that path is the J-curve: fees and undeployed or still-unmarked investments pull early IRRs down; realizations pull them up later. Do not compare a young fund’s IRR directly with a mature fund’s IRR. MOIC is a wealth multiple, not a rate of return; IRR puts time in.

why_wrong.A: MOIC is a wealth multiple and ignores time; it is not equal to IRR, and a low early IRR does not define MOIC.
why_wrong.C: The J-curve is about path and timing, not a permanent underperformance verdict.

AI-025.zh: J 曲線不是「另類一定先虧一輩子」。早期IRR 被call、費用、還沒實現的投資 往下拉，後來退出才往上彎。不要拿年輕基金的IRR 跟成熟基金比，更不要把IRR 跟MOIC 當成同一個數字。
AI-025.core_idea: The J-curve is early IRRs pulled down by calls, fees, and unmarked investments, then lifted by realizations
AI-025.study_section: Measuring Alternative Returns ｜另類報酬衡量
AI-025.source_note: 解答依據 AI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Alternative Investments。

AI-026.reasoning: Reasoning: MOIC = (realized value + unrealized value) / total invested capital = (80+40)/60 = 2.00×. It is a wealth multiple, not a rate of return. Invested capital in the notes is paid-in capital minus management fees and fund expenses. Given: Realized 80; unrealized 40; invested capital 60 (paid-in net of management fees and fund expenses). Asked: MOIC. Formula: MOIC = realized + unrealized invested capital Variables: Invested capital is paid-in minus management fees and fund expenses, not residual value. Why this formula: The ratio is total distributions plus residual value, relative to what was invested — a wealth multiple. Each unit of invested capital is now worth two units of realized-plus-residual value. Time is not in the ratio. Reasonableness check: 1.33× drops unrealized value. 3.00× double-counts capital in the numerator. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。

why_wrong.B: Adds invested capital into the numerator: (80+40+60)/60 = 3.00×.
why_wrong.C: Uses only realized value: 80/60 = 1.33×.

AI-026.zh: 分子是已實現加未實現，分母是投入資本：120/60=2.00×。不要只用已實現，也 不要把本金加回分子。MOIC 不管時間。

AI-027.reasoning: Reasoning: MOIC is a wealth multiple, not a rate of return. Evaluation uses IRR, a money multiple, and, when debt is used, a leveraged return on cash equity. IRR puts time in; MOIC does not. Equal multiples over unequal lives are not equal IRRs.

why_wrong.A: MOIC is not a rate of return and is not identical to IRR.
why_wrong.B: A longer wait for the same multiple produces a lower IRR, not a higher one.

AI-027.zh: 兩個都是1.80×，只代表財富倍數相同。花九年才走到同一個倍數，IRR 會比較 低。MOIC 不管時間，IRR 才把時間算進去。

AI-029.reasoning: Reasoning: Borrowing does not change the return on the assets. It changes the return on the cash the LP put up. r_L = r + (Vb/Vc)(r-rb) = 0.09 + (80/40)(0.09-0.05) = 0.09 + 2×0.04 = 17%. Check from cash: asset gain = 0.09×120 = 10.8; interest = 0.05×80 = 4.0; net 6.8 on 40 of equity →17%. If r>rb, leverage raises the return on cash. Given: Cash equity Vc=40; borrowing Vb=80 at rb=5%; unlevered return r=9% on the 120 position; interest is the only financing cost. Asked: Simple leveraged return on cash equity. Formula: rL = r + Vb Vc (r −rb) Variables: r is the periodic return on the position; rb the periodic borrowing rate; Vc cash equity; Vb amount borrowed. Why this formula: The cash investor earns r on every dollar in the position and pays rb only on the borrowed dollars. The extra per cash dollar is the spread (r-rb) scaled by Vb/Vc. Two borrowed dollars sit on each cash dollar. Each earns a 4% spread, so leverage adds 8 points to the 9% asset return. Reasonableness check: 9% is unlevered. 27% never subtracts the 5% borrowing rate. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。

why_wrong.A: Reports the unlevered asset return and ignores that the question asks for the cash-equity return.
why_wrong.C: Adds (Vb/Vc)×r without subtracting rb: 0.09+(80/40)×0.09=27%.

AI-029.zh: 槓桿多出來的是利差(9%-5%) 再乘借款／現金= 2×4%=8%，加回9% 得17%。 不要報資產報酬9%，也不要把借來的錢當成白賺同一個9%。

AI-030.reasoning: Reasoning: r_L = 0.03 + (50/50)(0.03-0.07) = 0.03 + 1×(-0.04) = -1.0%. If r<rb, leverage magnifies the loss. Cash check: asset gain 3, interest 3.5, net -0.5 on 50 of equity →-1%. The tempting +1% treats the 4-point gap as if borrowing were cheaper than the asset return. Given: Vc=50; Vb=50; rb=7%; r=3%; interest is the only financing cost. Asked: Simple leveraged return on cash equity. Formula: rL = r + Vb Vc (r −rb) Variables: The spread (r-rb) is negative when the assets earn less than the borrowing rate. Why this formula: Leverage scales the spread. A negative spread scaled by Vb/Vc pulls cash return below the already-low asset return. Borrowing at 7% to hold a 3% asset is a 4-point leak on each borrowed dollar. Reasonableness check: +3% is unlevered. +1% has the spread sign wrong. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。

why_wrong.A: Treats the 4-point gap between the 7% borrowing rate and the 3% asset return as a benefit, so the cash return comes out slightly positive instead of -1%.
why_wrong.B: Reports the unlevered 3% and ignores leverage on a position that earns less than the borrowing rate.

AI-030.zh: 資產只賺3%、借款要7%，利差是-4%。一倍槓桿把現金報酬打成-1%。不要把 符號翻成正的，也不要只報3%。

AI-031.reasoning: Reasoning: If r>rb, leverage raises the return on cash. If r<rb, it magnifies the loss. Breakeven is r_L=r, which occurs when r=rb: borrowing at the same rate the assets earn adds nothing. The cash investor earns r on every dollar and pays rb on borrowed dollars; those two cancel on the borrowed slice when the rates are equal.

why_wrong.A: When r=rb the interest exactly offsets the asset return earned on borrowed dollars, so there is no extra drag on the cash return beyond r.
why_wrong.B: Leverage raises cash return only when r>rb. Equality adds nothing.

AI-031.zh: 借錢利率剛好等於資產報酬時，借來的那一段賺的跟付出的利息打平，現金報酬 還是r。槓桿不是「借了就比較高」。

The equivalent cash identity is [r(Vc+Vb) - Vb rb]/Vc = [0.11×100 - 40×0.06]/60 = (11- 2.4)/60 = 8.6/60 = 14.3%. Same economics: earn 11 on the whole position, pay 2.4 of interest, residual 8.6 sits on 60 of cash. Given: Vc=60; Vb=40; rb=6%; r=11%; interest is the only financing cost. Asked: Simple leveraged return on cash equity. Formula: rL = r(Vc + Vb) −Vbrb Vc Variables: The two algebraic forms in the notes are identities, not two different returns. Why this formula: The numerator is asset gain minus interest; the denominator is cash equity only. Both forms must agree. If they do not, the spread or the interest dollar amount was dropped. Reasonableness check: 11% is unlevered. 18.3% treats borrowed dollars as earning r with no rb. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。

why_wrong.B: Adds (Vb/Vc)×r and never subtracts rb: 0.11+(40/60)×0.11=18.33%.

why_wrong.C: A close-out of a long sells toward the bid; covering a short buys toward the ask. The last print ignores that spread cost.

AI-035.zh: 保守收盤：多頭用買價（要賣出時拿到的），空頭用賣價（要回補時付出的）。反 過來是偏樂觀。中價是另一種做法，不是「最後成交一定無價差」。

why_wrong.B: The sources present both conventions; they do not require the midpoint.
why_wrong.C: The midpoint sits between bid and ask; it is not below the bid, and it is not more conservative than bid-long/ask-short.

AI-037.reasoning: Reasoning: Level 1: quoted price in an active market for an identical asset (exchange-traded public equity). Level 2: observable inputs other than Level 1 (an OTC rate derivative priced from quoted markets). Level 3: little or no market activity (private equity, real estate; a cash-flow model using market-participant assumptions).

why_wrong.A: That is Level 2: observable inputs other than Level 1.
why_wrong.B: That is Level 1: quoted price in an active market for an identical asset.

AI-037.zh: Level 3 是幾乎沒有市場活動：PE、不動產，用現金流模型。交易所股票是Level 1；用可觀察報價來的OTC 利率衍生性是Level 2。
AI-037.core_idea: Level 1 is an active-market quoted price; Level 2 other observable inputs; Level 3 little or no market activity

why_wrong.B: Bid-for-longs is the traded-book convention, not a rule that makes model marks more volatile than transactions.
why_wrong.C: Level 3 is little or no market activity — the opposite of “defined as transaction prices.”

AI-038.zh: 模型估價會把報酬報高、波動報低，軌跡看起來比較平滑。這不是「更保守所以 波動更大」，Level 3 更不是成交價本身。

why_wrong.B: Haircuts and dual NAVs are valuation choices; they do not replace NAV with MOIC or ban NAV.

AI-039.zh: 流動性差的券可以再打折。有些基金同時報交易NAV 與會計NAV。這不表示它 變成Level 1，也不表示不准報NAV。

AI-040.reasoning: Reasoning: Mark-to-model values tend to overstate reported returns and understate the volatility of those returns. The path looks smoother than the economics. Public-asset risk statistics often miss the risk that matters here. Survivorship and backfill separately pull averages up.

why_wrong.B: Survivorship bias pulls average returns up; it is not defined as understating volatility, and the mean is not thereby unbiased.
why_wrong.C: Conservative traded marks are bid for longs; model marks are the smoothing problem, and they do not mechanically inflate vol.

AI-040.zh: 模型NAV 把波動壓低，拿去跟上市股票一起做最適化，會把這檔基金當成比較安 全。存活者偏誤拉的是平均報酬，不是這個波動問題的定義。

AI-041.reasoning: Reasoning: Most private equity funds are leveraged buyout funds. The capital structure is primarily debt — bank debt, high-yield bonds, or mezzanine financing (subordinated debt or preferred shares, often with warrants or conversion features). Two smaller categories are distressed funds and developmental-capital funds.

why_wrong.A: CTAs running futures sit in macro/opportunistic hedge-fund strategies, not in LBO capital structure.
why_wrong.B: An LBO is a debt-funded purchase, not a public rights issue.

AI-041.zh: LBO 的資金結構以債為主：銀行貸、高收益債、或夾層（次順位債或特別股，常 帶認股權或轉換）。不是現金增資，也不是商品CTA。
AI-041.core_idea: Most PE funds are LBOs using primarily debt: bank debt, high-yield bonds, or mezzanine financing

AI-042.reasoning: Reasoning: High-cash-flow firms are attractive because that cash can service acquisition debt. A management buyout (MBO) keeps the existing team; a management buy-in (MBI) replaces it. Buyout targets are mature or in decline, in contrast to venture capital’s young companies.

why_wrong.A: High cash flow supports debt service; it does not forbid bank debt.
why_wrong.B: Seed-stage VC finances product development and marketing at a young firm, not a mature cash-cow buyout.

AI-042.zh: LBO 看重穩定現金流，是因為那筆現金要拿來還收購時借的債。這不是種子輪新 創，也不是「有現金就不能借錢」。
AI-042.core_idea: High-cash-flow firms are attractive in an LBO because that cash can service acquisition debt
AI-042.source_note: 解答依據 AI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Alternative Investments。

AI-043.reasoning: Reasoning: A management buyout (MBO) keeps the existing team; a management buy-in (MBI) replaces it. Both sit inside the LBO toolkit, not inside formative-stage VC.

why_wrong.A: An MBI replaces the existing team.
why_wrong.B: Angel / pre-seed is formative-stage venture capital for an idea and business plan, not a buyout of a mature firm.

AI-043.zh: MBO 留原班人馬；MBI 換掉管理層。種子天使輪是更早的創業投資，不是收購 成熟公司。
AI-043.core_idea: An MBO keeps the existing team; an MBI replaces it

AI-044.reasoning: Reasoning: Formative-stage investing is the earliest block: angel / pre-seed (typically individuals; idea and business plan); seed (VC capital for product development and marketing); early / start-up (initial commercial production and sales).

why_wrong.A: Mezzanine-stage is later: capital to prepare an already-operating firm for an IPO.
why_wrong.C: Later-stage / expansion is for a firm that is already operating and scaling, still before an IPO.

AI-044.zh: 天使／pre-seed 最早，多是個人對構想與計畫出資。擴張輪與上市前mezzaninestage 都晚得多。
AI-044.core_idea: Angel / pre-seed is typically individuals financing an idea and business plan
AI-044.source_note: 解答依據 AI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Alternative Investments。

AI-045.reasoning: Reasoning: Seed is VC capital for product development and marketing. Early / start-up is initial commercial production and sales. Those two sit inside formative-stage investing, after angel / pre-seed and before later-stage expansion.

why_wrong.A: Angel / pre-seed is typically individuals against an idea and plan, before institutional seed. Mezzanine-stage prepares an operating firm for an IPO.
why_wrong.B: Later-stage expansion scales an already-operating firm; a PIPE is private equity into a firm that is already public.

AI-045.zh: 種子輪做產品與行銷；早期／新創輪開始量產與銷售。天使更早，上市前 mezzanine-stage 與PIPE 都更晚、標的也不同。
AI-045.core_idea: Seed finances product development and marketing; early / start-up is initial commercial production and sales
AI-045.source_note: 解答依據 AI_answers_VERIFIED_V3_1.pdf；觀念依據講義 Alternative Investments。

AI-046.reasoning: Reasoning: Later-stage (expansion) financing is for a firm that is already operating and is scaling production and marketing, still before an IPO. Mezzanine-stage financing is capital provided to prepare the firm for an IPO; here “mezzanine” refers to timing, not to the subordinated-debt instrument of the same name.

why_wrong.A: Mezzanine-stage is specifically capital provided to prepare the firm for an IPO.

AI-075.reasoning: Reasoning: A commodity today and a commodity later are different goods. Owning the physical lot supplies use if needed; a futures contract defers delivery and avoids storage and the interest on tied-up cash. Convenience yield is the value of having the physical commodity during the life of the contract. The notes’ forms are F0(T)=S0 e^(r+c-i)T and F ≈S(1+rf)+storage-convenience yield.

why_wrong.A: Collateral yield is the return on margin collateral in the long-only futures attribution — not the value of holding the physical.
why_wrong.B: Roll yield is the gain or loss from replacing expiring contracts. It is related to curve shape, not defined as -convenience yield by name in the notes.

AI-076.reasoning: Reasoning: The discrete teaching form is F ≈S(1+rf)+storage-convenience yield = 50×1.04 + 3 - 1 = 52 + 3 - 1 = 54. The continuous form F0(T)=S0 e^(r+c-i)T is the same economics: finance and storage raise F; convenience yield lowers F. The notes treat the two forms as the same economics. Given: S=50; rf=4% over the life; storage=3; convenience yield=1. Asked: Approximate futures price from the discrete teaching form. Formula: F ≈S(1 + rf) + storage −convenience yield Variables: r_f finances tied-up cash; storage is the carry cost; convenience yield is the benefit of holding the physical. Why this formula: Owning the physical ties up cash and incurs storage, but supplies use. Futures defer delivery. The net of those pieces sets F relative to S. Carry (finance plus storage) exceeds convenience yield, so F sits above S — the contango side of the comparison. Reasonableness check: 52 omitted one of the carry pieces. 50 is the spot. 本題直接手算較快，不需要使用BA II Plus。
AI-076.steps: ①S(1+rf) = 50 × 1.04 = 52. ②Add storage 3: 55. Subtract convenience yield 1: 54.

why_wrong.A: Leaves the futures price at the spot, as if carry and convenience always cancel by rule.
why_wrong.B: Uses S(1+rf)=52 and drops both storage and convenience yield, or uses S+storage-CY=52 and drops the financing term.

AI-076.zh: 離散教學式：50×1.04=52，再加倉儲3、減便利收益1，得到54。只算52 是漏了 倉儲或漏了融資。現貨50 不是遠期。

AI-077.reasoning: Reasoning: If convenience yield is high — typically when inventories are low — the benefit of owning the physical exceeds carry cost. Spot is bid up relative to forward. S>F: backwardation, an inverted (downward-sloping) forward curve. If convenience yield is little or none, carry dominates. S<F: contango, an upward-sloping curve.

why_wrong.B: Convenience yield is the value of having the physical commodity, not a REIT concept.
why_wrong.C: Low inventories and high convenience yield are the backwardation case, not contango.

AI-078.reasoning: Reasoning: A long-only futures investor’s return splits into collateral yield, price return, and roll yield. Roll yield is positive in backwardation and negative in contango. Backwardation enhances the return of a long-only futures investor; contango reduces it. In contango the investor rolls into a richer deferred contract.

why_wrong.A: Collateral yield is the return on margin collateral — a separate piece of the three-way split.
why_wrong.B: That is the trap: treating higher deferred prices as the long’s gain. Those richer deferred prices are what the roller must buy.

AI-078.zh: 正價差時，到期要換成更貴的遠月，roll 是負的。看到遠月比較高就以為多方在 賺，是把「必須買進的價格」當成收益。擔保品收益是另一項。

AI-079.reasoning: Reasoning: In backwardation the expiring contract sits above the deferred contract, so rolling into the next contract is a roll down the curve — positive roll yield. In contango the investor rolls into a richer deferred contract — negative roll yield. The mechanism is the roll, not a story about the curve looking cheap.

why_wrong.A: Contango is the case that reduces long-only return. The long is not “selling the curve”; the long is buying the next contract.
why_wrong.C: Low convenience yield is the usual contango description; the roll is negative, not zero.

AI-079.zh: 逆價差：近月貴、遠月便宜，換月是貴的換成便宜的，對長期做多有利。正價差 相反。便利收益率低不是roll 等於零。

AI-080.reasoning: Reasoning: Higher deferred prices look like a richer market. For someone who is already long and must roll, those higher deferred prices are the contracts that must be bought as near contracts expire. Negative roll yield is the cost of that roll. The long-only result is the opposite of the first impression: contango reduces the return; backwardation enhances it.

why_wrong.A: The long who is already long and must roll buys the deferred contract; the candidate has the buy/sell sides reversed.
why_wrong.C: The three components stay separate. Contango does not redefine price return as collateral yield.

AI-080.zh: 遠月比較貴，看起來像市場更豐厚；但長期做多換月時買的就是那個更貴的合約。 正價差對long-only 是成本，不是收益。

why_wrong.B: The three pieces are separate. Spot can rise in contango; the roll is still the cost of buying a richer deferred contract.
why_wrong.C: Collateral yield is the return on margin collateral, not a restatement of the spot change.

AI-081.zh: 現貨可以漲（price return 為正），同時曲線仍是正價差（roll 為負）。三項不會自 動同號。擔保品收益是保證金現金的報酬，不是現貨漲跌。

why_wrong.B: Convenience yield exceeding carry is the backwardation case (spot bid up). Contango is carry dominating, little or no convenience yield.
why_wrong.C: Upward-sloping is S<F, contango — not backwardation. Backwardation is inverted, S>F.

AI-084.reasoning: Reasoning: A hedge fund is typically a limited partnership. Investors need sufficient wealth, liquidity, and sophistication. The GP usually charges both a management fee and an incentive fee, and managers are typically required to invest their own capital. Regulation is light; ownership is private; horizons are often short. Hedge funds may use leverage, long and short positions, derivatives, and illiquid assets. They do not necessarily hedge.

why_wrong.C: Hedge funds do not necessarily hedge. Matched-pair hedging is one possible subset (equity hedge / relative value), not the definition.

AI-084.zh: 對沖基金是結構與工具箱（合夥、2 和20、可多空槓桿衍生性），不是「一定有對 沖」。它在流動性梯子的左邊，不是共同基金。

AI-086.reasoning: Reasoning: Event-driven: a restructuring or acquisition. Subsets: merger arbitrage (long the target), distressed, activist, special situations. Relative value longs one security and shorts a related one, waiting for a pricing gap to close. Macro / opportunistic trades global economic views. Equity hedge is long and/or short public equities and equity derivatives.

why_wrong.A: Long the target is a long (merger-arb) position, not short bias.
why_wrong.C: Macro / opportunistic trades global economic views across equities, bonds, currencies, or commodities — not a single-deal spread.

AI-086.zh: 事件驅動做重整或併購；合併套利是做多標的、等價差收斂。這不是總體觀點， 也不是空頭偏向。

AI-087.reasoning: Reasoning: Relative value: long one security and short a related one, waiting for a pricing gap to close. Convertible arbitrage, asset-backed and general fixed-income arbitrage, volatility, multistrategy. The pair can still lose if the gap widens or if financing fails; “relative” is not “hedged by definition.”

why_wrong.A: Convertible arbitrage is relative value, not market-neutral equity hedge. The short stock hedges the bond’s equity option, not a zero-beta equity book.
why_wrong.B: Merger arbitrage is event-driven; a convertible-versus-stock pricing gap is relative value, not a deal-spread.

AI-087.zh: 相對價值是一邊多、一邊空相關證券，等價差收掉。可轉債套利是這一族。不是 維權事件，也不是商品CTA。
AI-087.core_idea: Relative value is long one security and short a related one, waiting for a pricing gap to close

AI-088.reasoning: Reasoning: Macro / opportunistic: global economic views; long or short equities, bonds, currencies, or commodities. Managed futures (CTAs following commodity momentum) sit here. Equity hedge: long and/or short public equities and equity derivatives (market neutral, fundamental growth, fundamental value, quantitative directional, short bias).

why_wrong.C: Equity-hedge fundamental value is a public-equity style, not a CTA commodity book.

AI-088.zh: 商品動量CTA 歸在總體／機會型。不是合併套利，也不是股票基本面價值對沖。
AI-088.core_idea: Macro / opportunistic trades global views; managed futures (CTAs following commodity momentum) sit here

why_wrong.A: CTA / managed-futures momentum is macro, not a listed-equity short-bias book.
why_wrong.B: Short bias is a directional equity-hedge subset; market-neutral aims to strip market beta, not to keep a net short.

why_wrong.B: ETF is the most liquid end of the ladder (LP →SMA →closed-end →mutual fund →ETF), not the least, and a FoF is not automatically an ETF.

AI-092.reasoning: Reasoning: A distributed ledger is a shared database. Distributed ledger technology (DLT) is the stack used to improve delivery of financial services. Tokenization represents ownership rights to a physical asset on a blockchain or other distributed ledger.

AI-093.reasoning: Reasoning: A blockchain records information sequentially in blocks that are cryptographically linked. Each block holds a batch of entries and a hash to the previous block. New blocks join only after a consensus protocol. Proof of work and proof of stake are two such protocols.

why_wrong.A: Permissioned networks still use a consensus protocol among approved nodes; an allow-list is not a substitute for consensus.
why_wrong.B: PoW is one consensus design; appending a block still requires the network’s consensus rule, not hashing in isolation.

AI-093.zh: 新區塊要先通過共識協議才接得上去。這跟瀑布分配、高水位或Level 3 估價不是 同一件事。

AI-094.reasoning: Reasoning: Proof of work: miners compete in a computationally costly lottery over which block is added; the longest chain is costly to rewrite in a short time. Proof of stake: validators pledge capital to vouch for a block.

why_wrong.A: Futures carry is a commodity-pricing idea; it is not how validators append blocks.
why_wrong.B: Catch-up is a partnership distribution clause, not a consensus protocol.

AI-094.zh: 工作量證明是礦工用算力抽籤搶記帳；權益證明是驗證者押資本為區塊背書。不 要寫成GP 追補或商品便利收益率。

why_wrong.B: Restricted participation is the permissioned design, not the permissionless one.
why_wrong.C: Permissionless networks do not require an admitting administrator; that access control is the permissioned design.
